_**Some Sexy Songs 4 U**_ (stylized as _**$ome $exy $ongs 4 U**_ or shortened to _**$$$4U**_)[\[2\]](#cite_note-$$$-2) is a collaborative studio album by Canadian musicians [PartyNextDoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor "PartyNextDoor") and [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)"). It was released on February 14, 2025, by [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound"), Santa Anna, and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"). The album features guest appearances from [Pimmie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pimmie "Pimmie"), [Yebba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yebba "Yebba"), and [Chino Pacas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chino_Pacas "Chino Pacas"). Production on the album was handled by PartyNextDoor and Drake's frequent collaborators [Noel Cadastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound"), [Gordo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordo_\(DJ\) "Gordo (DJ)"), and Jordan Ullman of [Majid Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majid_Jordan "Majid Jordan"), among others.

Originally set to release in late-2024, _Some Sexy Songs 4 U_ was delayed several times. The album serves as a follow-up to the artists' respective studio albums _[PartyNextDoor 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor_4 "PartyNextDoor 4")_ (2024) and _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_ (2023). It marks PartyNextDoor's first collaborative project and Drake's third, after 2015's _[What a Time to Be Alive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_a_Time_to_Be_Alive "What a Time to Be Alive")_ (with [Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_\(rapper\) "Future (rapper)")) and 2022's _[Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss "Her Loss")_ (with [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage")). The album was released among the backdrop of Drake's ongoing legal dispute with [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") (UMG) and was his first full-length release following [his feud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake–Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud") with [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar"). _Some Sexy Songs 4 U_ was supported by four singles, including "[Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_\(song\) "Nokia (song)")" and "[Die Trying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_Trying_\(PartyNextDoor,_Drake,_and_Yebba_song\) "Die Trying (PartyNextDoor, Drake, and Yebba song)")". The pair embarked on the [Some Special Shows 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Special_Shows_4_U "Some Special Shows 4 U") tour in support of the album.

_Some Sexy Songs 4 U_ opened with first-week sales of 246,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_units "Album-equivalent units") in the United States and debuted at number one on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), marking PartyNextDoor's first chart-topper and Drake's fourteenth, tying him with [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z") and [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") for the most number-one albums on the chart by solo artists. It also topped the [albums chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Canadian_Albums "Billboard Canadian Albums") in the artists' native of Canada. Internationally, it peaked in the top ten in Australia, Belgium, the Netherlands, Ireland, Lithuania, New Zealand, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Upon its release, the album received mixed reviews from critics, who praised its production and intimate nature, but criticized the runtime and lyricism.

The album follows the pair's numerous collaborations since PartyNextDoor was signed to Drake's record label, [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound"), back in 2013, with the first of these being Drake's guest appearance on "Over Here" from PartyNextDoor's [eponymous mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor_\(mixtape\) "PartyNextDoor (mixtape)") (2013).[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) Alongside their collaborations, they have contributed to each other's individual songs as a writer or producer.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) PartyNextDoor supported the release of his album _[PartyNextDoor 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor_4 "PartyNextDoor 4")_ (2024) through a twenty-four-stop Canada and U.S. live tour.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) On August 2, 2024, at the tour's stop at the [Budweiser Stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budweiser_Stage "Budweiser Stage") in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto")—the artists' hometown—Drake performed as a surprise guest, with his set foregoing any of the hip-hop tracks in his discography.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) He then announced the collaborative album, saying, "On behalf of me and Party, we've been working on something for y'all. So, you get the summer over with, you do what you need to do. I know all you girls are outside. When it gets a little chilly, PartyNextDoor and Drake album will be waiting right there for you".[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

Just two days later, the OVO [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") page seemingly hinted at the album by posting backstage pictures of Drake and PartyNextDoor that was taken after the concert.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) During an interview on August 5, PartyNextDoor revealed that his favorite collaboration with Drake "\[are\] the \[ones\] we \[are\] doing right now. All 15 of them", seemingly revealing that the pair were working on 15 songs for the album.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) On August 6, Drake released 100 gigabytes of data, including behind-the-scenes clips, tour rehearsals, and studio footage. He also previewed three unreleased tracks (tracks of which what would later be released as the _[100 Gigs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/100_Gigs "100 Gigs")_) under an Instagram page by the name "plottttwistttttt".[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) On August 7, video clips surfaced of nightclubs in Canada previewing unreleased music from the album.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) On the same day, via the "plottttwistttttt" Instagram account, Drake reposted a tweet, blurring out the words "album rollout" regarding another unheard track.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

On October 5, Drake attended at [Tyrone Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrone_Edwards "Tyrone Edwards")' Nostalgia Party in Toronto, where he called out his "fake friends" in the music industry and cited PartyNextDoor as a "real" friend. He also hinted at the album's impending release by saying "shoutout to my brother PX, album dropping soon".[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) In an appearance on _The Fry Yiy Show_ on [SiriusXM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SiriusXM "SiriusXM") that same month, OVO engineer, [Noel Cadastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noel_Cadastre "Noel Cadastre"), stated that the album only required "finishing touches" and called November "a jam-packed month for me \[to finish the album\]". PartyNextDoor then revealed work on the album would continue after the conclusion of the European leg of his Sorry I'm Outside Tour on November 6, saying, "I have one more show on this tour, then the album is getting finished".[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) During a [Kick live stream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick_\(service\) "Kick (service)") with [xQc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XQc "XQc") on November 24, Drake stated the album was almost complete, saying, "\[the\] album is 75 percent done. Shout out to PX, cooking right now," and added that "the album sounds incredible... It's the sound people know and love us for".[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) On December 26, Drake appeared on a Kick live stream with [Adin Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adin_Ross "Adin Ross"), in which he stated that the album is one of the records that he is "most proud of in \[his\] life". He also revealed that the album was supposed to release in November, but was delayed.[\[23\]](#cite_note-:01-23)

_Some Sexy Songs 4 U_'s release follows legal action by Drake against [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") (UMG), the parent company of [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"), with whom Drake has a [recording contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_contract "Recording contract"). In November 2024, Drake initiated a legal petition against UMG and [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") in the U.S., alleging they conspired to artificially inflate the number of streams of the [diss track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diss_track "Diss track"), "[Not Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us "Not Like Us")" by [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") on the service during Drake's [feud with Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake–Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud") earlier that year by implementing [pay-to-play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payola "Payola"), [malicious bots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_bot#Malicious_bots "Internet bot"), and other tactics.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) Drake withdrew the petition on January 14, 2025, and filed a [lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawsuit "Lawsuit") in U.S. district court a day later, alleging [defamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defamation "Defamation") against UMG for promoting "Not Like Us".[\[25\]](#cite_note-Variety-25) This legal dispute caused confusion regarding which label or company would act as the distributor for _Some Sexy Songs 4 U_.[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)[\[27\]](#cite_note-Skit-27) It was eventually released through OVO, Santa Anna, and Republic, each of which are the artists' labels, while it was distributed through Santa Anna (owned by [Sony Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music "Sony Music")), but licensed to Republic.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)

On February 3, 2025, the album's title was revealed and its release date of February 14 was announced.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) The announcement included a snippet of "Deeper".[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)[\[2\]](#cite_note-$$$-2) On February 9, Drake shared a snippet of the song "Crying in Chanel".[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) A day later, Drake shared a promotional skit for the album starring the Canadian comedic duo Jermaine and Trevaunn Richards, which depicted Trevaunn practicing a romantic speech with his brother for his girlfriend but being unable or unwilling to tell her that he loves her. According to Jon Powell of [Revolt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolt_TV "Revolt TV"), this exemplifies the "playful, self-aware marketing that helped Drake maintain his cultural dominance for well over a decade".[\[27\]](#cite_note-Skit-27) Drake previously collaborated with the Richards by making a cameo appearance in the duo's "T-Dot Goon Scrap DVD 2" comedy sketch in May 2017.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

The following day, Drake shared the album's official cover art via Instagram,[\[33\]](#cite_note-Artwork-33) which depicted Drake (left) and PartyNextDoor (right) standing together during a snowstorm in front of [Absolute World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_World "Absolute World") in [Mississauga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississauga "Mississauga"), Ontario, wearing oversized fur coats.[\[33\]](#cite_note-Artwork-33)[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) On February 12, Drake shared a snippet of the track "[Somebody Loves Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somebody_Loves_Me_\(PartyNextDoor_and_Drake_song\) "Somebody Loves Me (PartyNextDoor and Drake song)")" on "@plottttwistttttt".[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) He also shared a photo of the title page of December 2024-draft of a [screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenplay "Screenplay") called "$$$ 4 U" (the acronym for the album title): it listed Drake and PartyNextDoor as its writers and that it was based on an unreleased novel of the same name by Drake's father, Dennis Graham.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) A day later, Drake revealed the album's 21-song tracklist via Instagram and confirmed its runtime to be 74 minutes.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37)

In October 2025, PartyNextDoor released _$$$_, a short film inspired by the album.[\[38\]](#cite_note-38)

On February 13, 2025, some social media users and [Freddie Gibbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Gibbs "Freddie Gibbs") accused Drake and PartyNextDoor of plagiarizing use of the dollar symbol in the album's title and bunnies in its promotional material from Gibbs' album _[Soul Sold Separately](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_Sold_Separately "Soul Sold Separately")_ (2022).[\[39\]](#cite_note-39)[\[40\]](#cite_note-40)[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) Canadian rapper John River accused Drake and PartyNextDoor of plagiarizing the pose in front of Absolute World in the album's artwork from his music video to his 2021 single "Hope City II": he claimed PartyNextDoor and "another OVO artist" contacted him "obsessing" over his video and "thought process", but threatened to [blackball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blacklisting "Blacklisting") him after River refused to act as a [ghostwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghostwriter "Ghostwriter").[\[42\]](#cite_note-:0-42)[\[43\]](#cite_note-43)

## Music and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Some_Sexy_Songs_4_U&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Music and composition")\]

_Some Sexy Songs 4 U_ contains twenty-one tracks, with a playing time of over 73 minutes.[\[44\]](#cite_note-TNYT-44)[\[45\]](#cite_note-45) Its album release coincides with [Valentine's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentine's_Day "Valentine's Day"), marking Drake's third full-length project to be released near that date, after _[So Far Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_Far_Gone_\(mixtape\) "So Far Gone (mixtape)")_ (2009) and _[If You're Reading This It's Too Late](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_You're_Reading_This_It's_Too_Late "If You're Reading This It's Too Late")_ (2015); according to _[HotNewHipHop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HotNewHipHop "HotNewHipHop")_, Drake's albums released during this time "reflect his shifting perspectives on love, success, and emotional vulnerability", saying, "Few artists have aligned themselves with a holiday like Drake has with Valentine's Day".[\[46\]](#cite_note-46)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Noah_Shebib.jpg/250px-Noah_Shebib.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Noah_Shebib.jpg)

_Some Sexy Songs 4 U_ is Drake's first album to not include longtime collaborator and friend [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40_\(producer\) "40 (producer)") as a producer.

According to Will Schube and Kia Turner of _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_Networks "Complex Networks")_, _Some Sexy Songs 4 U_ primarily mixes elements of [contemporary R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B"), [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), and [trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music "Trap music").[\[47\]](#cite_note-Clash-47)[\[48\]](#cite_note-Complex-48) It also explores [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock"), [acoustic pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"),[\[48\]](#cite_note-Complex-48) and [regional Mexican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_Mexican "Regional Mexican") on certain songs.[\[44\]](#cite_note-TNYT-44) The album features production from several different producers, which was handled primarily by Drake's longtime collaborators [Noel Cadastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noel_Cadastre "Noel Cadastre"), [Gordo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordo_\(DJ\) "Gordo (DJ)"), [Jordan Ullman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majid_Jordan "Majid Jordan") and PartyNextDoor himself, alongside PartyNextDoor's frequent collaborators Alex Lustig, Niketaz, and Niko.[\[49\]](#cite_note-49)

According to Joe Coscarelli of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_, the lyrical themes on the album are reminiscent of both Drake and PartyNextDoor's previous works, including Drake's _[Dark Lane Demo Tapes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Lane_Demo_Tapes "Dark Lane Demo Tapes")_ (2020) and PartyNextDoor's _[PartyNextDoor 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor_3 "PartyNextDoor 3")_ (2016).[\[44\]](#cite_note-TNYT-44) On the album, Drake takes several shots at other artists, including [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") and [Joe Budden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Budden "Joe Budden"), while he makes references to [Charli XCX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charli_XCX "Charli XCX") and her album _[Brat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brat_\(album\) "Brat (album)")_ (2024), [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage"), and [Tate McRae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tate_McRae "Tate McRae").[\[50\]](#cite_note-NME-50)

Throughout the record, "Drake's attention remains primarily on the ladies" while PartyNextDoor "opens up about his sexual escapades", according to _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Carl Lamarre and Michael Saponara.[\[51\]](#cite_note-BB_Ranked-51) Drake covers the topics of a [bachelor lifestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor "Bachelor"), settling down, being turned on by his peers, and his previous sexual experiences.[\[51\]](#cite_note-BB_Ranked-51)[\[52\]](#cite_note-Vibe-52) Similarly, PartyNextDoor covers themes of sex, money, [infidelity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infidelity "Infidelity"), and [sexual jealousy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_jealousy "Sexual jealousy").[\[51\]](#cite_note-BB_Ranked-51)[\[52\]](#cite_note-Vibe-52)

# Her Loss

ion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megan_Thee_Stallion "Megan Thee Stallion");[\[62\]](#cite_note-XXL_Ech_2022-62)
    *   interpolations of "[24's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24's_\(T.I._song\) "24's (T.I. song)")",[\[63\]](#cite_note-Saponara_BB_2022-63) written by [Clifford Harris Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T.I. "T.I.") and [Aldrin Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Toomp "DJ Toomp"), as performed by [T.I.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T.I. "T.I.").
*   "Major Distribution" contains samples of "East Village", written by Elijah Fox-Peck and performed by [Elijah Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elijah_Fox "Elijah Fox").
*   "Privileged Rappers" contains samples of "Ballad for the Fallen Soldier", written by [Ronald Isley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Isley "Ronald Isley"), [O'Kelly Isley Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O'Kelly_Isley_Jr. "O'Kelly Isley Jr."), [Rudolph Isley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudolph_Isley "Rudolph Isley"), [Ernie Isley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernie_Isley "Ernie Isley"), [Marvin Isley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Isley "Marvin Isley"), and [Chris Jasper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Jasper "Chris Jasper"), as performed by [the Isley Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Isley_Brothers "The Isley Brothers").
*   "Spin Bout U" contains samples of "Give Me Your Lov-N", written by Tenaia Sanders and Dwayne Armstrong, as performed by Oobie.[\[64\]](#cite_note-GQ_HL_2022-64)
*   "Hours in Silence" contains samples of "Stash Pot", written by [Paul Beauregard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Paul "DJ Paul") and performed by Koopsta Knicca.
*   "Treacherous Twins" contains samples of "Lonely Daze", written by [Elgin Lumpkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginuwine "Ginuwine"), [Timothy Mosley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbaland "Timbaland"), [Melvin Barcliff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbaland_&_Magoo "Timbaland & Magoo"), [Thom Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thom_Bell "Thom Bell"), and [Linda Creed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Creed "Linda Creed"), as performed by [Ginuwine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginuwine "Ginuwine").
*   "Circo Loco" contains elements of "[One More Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_More_Time_\(Daft_Punk_song\) "One More Time (Daft Punk song)")", written by [Thomas Bangalter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Bangalter "Thomas Bangalter"), [Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy-Manuel_de_Homem-Christo "Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo"), and [Anthony Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanthony "Romanthony"), as performed by [Daft Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daft_Punk "Daft Punk").[\[65\]](#cite_note-PF_MB_2022-65)
*   "Middle of the Ocean" contains samples of:
    *   "Real Niggas", written by [Cameron Giles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cam'ron "Cam'ron"), [Joseph Jones II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Jones_\(rapper\) "Jim Jones (rapper)"), [LaRon James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juelz_Santana "Juelz Santana"), and Darryl Pittman, as performed by [the Diplomats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Diplomats "The Diplomats");
    *   and "Cry Together", written by [Kenneth Gamble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamble_and_Huff "Gamble and Huff") and [Leon Huff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamble_and_Huff "Gamble and Huff"), as performed by [the O'Jays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_O'Jays "The O'Jays").

Credits adapted from official liner notes.[\[66\]](#cite_note-66)

**Musicians**

*   [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") – vocals (tracks 1–14, 16)
*   [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage") – vocals (1–3, 5–11, 14, 15)
*   [Travis Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Scott "Travis Scott") – vocals (10)
*   [Birdman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birdman_\(rapper\) "Birdman (rapper)") – additional vocals (1, 12)
*   [Young Nudy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Nudy "Young Nudy") – additional vocals (1)
*   [Tay Keith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tay_Keith "Tay Keith") – drums (1, 9)
*   [Vinylz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinylz "Vinylz") – drums (1, 9)
*   [Elijah Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elijah_Fox "Elijah Fox") – additional vocals (2)
*   Big Bank – additional vocals (3)
*   [Lil Yachty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Yachty "Lil Yachty") – additional vocals (4), background vocals (13)
*   [Noah Shebib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40_\(record_producer\) "40 (record producer)") – additional keyboards (5)
*   Noel Cadastre – drums, keyboards (8)
*   [Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz_\(record_producer\) "Oz (record producer)") – drums (8)
*   Dougie F – background vocals (16)

**Technical**

*   Chris Athens – [mastering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastering_\(audio\) "Mastering (audio)")
*   Dave Huffman – mastering (1–8), mastering assistance (9–16)
*   Noah Shebib – [mixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mixing_\(recorded_music\) "Audio mixing (recorded music)") (all tracks)
*   Noel Cadastre – mixing (1–13, 15, 16), recording (1–7, 10–16), mixing assistance (14)
*   [Metro Boomin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Boomin "Metro Boomin") – mixing (14)
*   Ethan Stevens – mixing (14), recording (10)
*   Les Bateman – engineering
*   Isaiah Brown – recording (1–3, 5–7, 11, 14, 15)
*   Harley Arsenault – mixing assistance (1–13, 15, 16)
*   Greg Moffet – mixing assistance (1, 9–16)

# Nokia (song)

["Nokia"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8ekJMC8OtGU) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_\(identifier\) "YouTube video (identifier)")

"**Nokia**" (stylized in [all caps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_caps "All caps")) is a song by Canadian rapper [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") from his collaborative studio album with [PartyNextDoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor "PartyNextDoor") entitled _[Some Sexy Songs 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Sexy_Songs_4_U "Some Sexy Songs 4 U")_.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) Written by Drake and produced by Paul Omar "Elkan" Agyei, it was released on February 14, 2025, by Santa Anna Label Group, [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"). It impacted [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") as the album's second single on March 11, 2025. "Nokia" peaked at number five on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100") and number two on the [Billboard Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") on April 19, 2025. Outside of North America, "Nokia" peaked within the top ten of the charts in Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom.

The beat is described as a "sweaty Atlanta bass beat peppered with flashy synths" with "androgynous vocals" (by Elkan).[\[4\]](#cite_note-PF-4) In the second half of the song, "the beat stutters and slows into a crunchy groove" and Drake raps in a "[Whodini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whodini "Whodini")\-type flow".[\[4\]](#cite_note-PF-4) The synth sounds sample the well-known Nokia ringtone from the 1990s and early 2000s.

The song received positive reviews. _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Michael Saponara ranked the song as the fifth best track on _Some Sexy Songs 4 U_.[\[5\]](#cite_note-BB_Ranked-5) Saponara wrote that the track is an "electronic banger that has girls running around with glowstick necklaces" while stating that it would make "[Daft Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daft_Punk "Daft Punk") proud".[\[5\]](#cite_note-BB_Ranked-5) He also stated that the track "showcases the supreme innovator" within Drake.[\[5\]](#cite_note-BB_Ranked-5) _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")_'s Mano Sundaresan wrote that the song "immediately feels ready for a drunken karaoke night" while describing it as an "indulgent, fan-service record".[\[4\]](#cite_note-PF-4)

_[HotNewHipHop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HotNewHipHop "HotNewHipHop")_ ranked the song as the 4th best rap song of 2025.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

The song's official music video was released on March 31, 2025. It was deleted moments after its upload on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), however, it was soon reuploaded.[\[7\]](#cite_note-ComplexVid-7) The video was shot in [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX"), was directed by Theo Skudra, and features a cameo from [Shai Gilgeous-Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shai_Gilgeous-Alexander "Shai Gilgeous-Alexander").[\[7\]](#cite_note-ComplexVid-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) Described as "nostalgic" by _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_'s Tomás Mier, the video is black-and-white and features [Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia "Nokia")'s famous [snake game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_\(1998_video_game\) "Snake (1998 video game)").[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Michael Saponara wrote that Drake "invites a crew of girls for a Carnival-themed celebration before switching his focus to beautiful women flanking him for a night of rollerblading".[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

# Nokia (song)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

"Nokia"

[Single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_\(music\) "Single (music)") by [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)")

from the album _[Some Sexy Songs 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Sexy_Songs_4_U "Some Sexy Songs 4 U")_

Released

March 11, 2025

[Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_studio "Recording studio")

*   S.O.T.A (Florida)
*   Sanctuary ([Nassau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nassau,_The_Bahamas "Nassau, The Bahamas"))

[Genre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre "Music genre")

*   [Hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop")[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)
*   [pop rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rap "Pop rap")[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

Length

4:01

[Label](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_label "Record label")

*   Santa Anna
*   [OVO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound")
*   [Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records")

[Songwriters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriter "Songwriter")

*   [Aubrey Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)")
*   Paul Agyei

[Producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_producer "Record producer")

Elkan

[Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") singles chronology

"[Somebody Loves Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somebody_Loves_Me_\(PartyNextDoor_and_Drake_song\) "Somebody Loves Me (PartyNextDoor and Drake song)")"  
(2025)

Music video

["Nokia"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8ekJMC8OtGU) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_\(identifier\) "YouTube video (identifier)")

"**Nokia**" (stylized in [all caps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_caps "All caps")) is a song by Canadian rapper [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") from his collaborative studio album with [PartyNextDoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor "PartyNextDoor") entitled _[Some Sexy Songs 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Sexy_Songs_4_U "Some Sexy Songs 4 U")_.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) Written by Drake and produced by Paul Omar "Elkan" Agyei, it was released on February 14, 2025, by Santa Anna Label Group, [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"). It impacted [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") as the album's second single on March 11, 2025. "Nokia" peaked at number five on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100") and number two on the [Billboard Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") on April 19, 2025. Outside of North America, "Nokia" peaked within the top ten of the charts in Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom.

The beat is described as a "sweaty Atlanta bass beat peppered with flashy synths" with "androgynous vocals" (by Elkan).[\[4\]](#cite_note-PF-4) In the second half of the song, "the beat stutters and slows into a crunchy groove" and Drake raps in a "[Whodini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whodini "Whodini")\-type flow".[\[4\]](#cite_note-PF-4) The synth sounds sample the well-known Nokia ringtone from the 1990s and early 2000s.

The song received positive reviews. _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Michael Saponara ranked the song as the fifth best track on _Some Sexy Songs 4 U_.[\[5\]](#cite_note-BB_Ranked-5) Saponara wrote that the track is an "electronic banger that has girls running around with glowstick necklaces" while stating that it would make "[Daft Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daft_Punk "Daft Punk") proud".[\[5\]](#cite_note-BB_Ranked-5) He also stated that the track "showcases the supreme innovator" within Drake.[\[5\]](#cite_note-BB_Ranked-5) _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")_'s Mano Sundaresan wrote that the song "immediately feels ready for a drunken karaoke night" while describing it as an "indulgent, fan-service record".[\[4\]](#cite_note-PF-4)

_[HotNewHipHop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HotNewHipHop "HotNewHipHop")_ ranked the song as the 4th best rap song of 2025.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

The song's official music video was released on March 31, 2025. It was deleted moments after its upload on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), however, it was soon reuploaded.[\[7\]](#cite_note-ComplexVid-7) The video was shot in [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX"), was directed by Theo Skudra, and features a cameo from [Shai Gilgeous-Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shai_Gilgeous-Alexander "Shai Gilgeous-Alexander").[\[7\]](#cite_note-ComplexVid-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) Described as "nostalgic" by _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_'s Tomás Mier, the video is black-and-white and features [Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia "Nokia")'s famous [snake game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_\(1998_video_game\) "Snake (1998 video game)").[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Michael Saponara wrote that Drake "invites a crew of girls for a Carnival-themed celebration before switching his focus to beautiful women flanking him for a night of rollerblading".[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

**Musicians**

**Technical**

*   Dave Huffman – assistant mastering engineer

# First Person Shooter (song)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

"First Person Shooter"

[Single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_\(music\) "Single (music)") by [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") featuring [J. Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Cole "J. Cole")

from the album _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_

October 24, 2023

October 5, 2023

[Genre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre "Music genre")

*   [Hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music")
*   [trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music "Trap music")

4:07

*   [OVO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound")

"**First Person Shooter**" is a song by Canadian rapper [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") featuring American rapper [J. Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Cole "J. Cole"). It was released through [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") on Drake's eighth studio album, _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_. Drake and Cole wrote the song with producers [Boi-1da](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boi-1da "Boi-1da"), [Vinylz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinylz "Vinylz"), [Tay Keith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tay_Keith "Tay Keith"), [FnZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FnZ "FnZ") (Michael Mulé and Isaac De Boni), [Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz_\(record_producer\) "Oz (record producer)"), and Coleman, alongside Snorre Tidemand. It is notable for reigniting Drake's [decade-long feud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake–Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud") with fellow rapper [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar").

"First Person Shooter" debuted at number one on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), becoming Drake's thirteenth and Cole's first number-one song. It later impacted US [rhythmic radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_radio "Rhythmic radio") on October 24, 2023, as the album's fourth single. Its music video was released on November 15, 2023.

During a _Table for One_ special episode on October 6, 2023, a few hours before _For All the Dogs_ was released, Drake confirmed that J. Cole would appear on the sixth track of the album, calling it "fourth quarter magic", and also revealed that he and Cole had "just got out from the studio",[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) making it the final song to be recorded for the album.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

"First Person Shooter" features a "subtle-yet-triumphant"[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard-3) yet "high-octane" production that starts out with a "warped" vocal sample of Joe Washington's "Look Me in the Eyes"[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) while both artists exchange a few bars. The second half of the song features a down-pitched looped sample from Snorre Tidemand's orchestral "Redemption."[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) The "hard" and "playful" track was especially noted for its "futuristic and energetic" production that enabled Drake and Cole to showcase their skills.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) The track sees Cole reflecting on his continuous success, arguing that him, Drake, and fellow American rapper [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") are the "big three" in rap music whereas he himself feels like [Muhammad Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ali "Muhammad Ali"). Another reference includes a comparison of both artists to a [meme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_meme "Internet meme") of two [Spider-Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man "Spider-Man") pointing at each other. Cole also says that he wishes to collaborate with fellow American rapper [YoungBoy Never Broke Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YoungBoy_Never_Broke_Again "YoungBoy Never Broke Again") later on the song, seemingly dismissing rumors of him dissing the rapper on his collaboration with rapper and album producer [Lil Yachty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Yachty "Lil Yachty") on "[The Secret Recipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Secret_Recipe "The Secret Recipe")", while he also confirms that his upcoming album, _The Fall Off_, is on the way.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) In reference to his fame and commercial success, Drake later shouts out Michael Jackson, notably referencing how he was one song away from eventually tying the latter's record for most number-one US _Billboard_ Hot 100 singles by a solo male artist.[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard-3)

### Response from Kendrick Lamar

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=First_Person_Shooter_\(song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Response from Kendrick Lamar")\]

After hearing of J. Cole's "big three" lyrical claim, rapper [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") appeared on [Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_\(rapper\) "Future (rapper)") and [Metro Boomin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Boomin "Metro Boomin")'s single, "[Like That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like_That_\(Future,_Metro_Boomin_and_Kendrick_Lamar_song\) "Like That (Future, Metro Boomin and Kendrick Lamar song)")", which was released in late-March 2024.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) On his verse, he responds to Cole and Drake, rapping "Motherfuck the big three, nigga, it's just big me."[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

In a first assessment of the album, Kyle Denis of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ ranked "First Person Shooter" as the ninth best track of the album, writing that the duo had adopted an "elder statesmen" mentality while still presenting their "skin in the game", but while their attitude was seen as "braggadocious", both were holding back a little.[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard-3) _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_'s Mosi Reeves stated that on the song, Drake is "thoroughly outclassed by J Cole" and that his lyrics are basic, several of them being "desultory lyrics where he discusses women like he’s stocking a meat freezer."[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) Writing for _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_\(magazine\) "Clash (magazine)")_, Shahzaib Hussain notes that "First Person Shooter" sees Drake "all shit-talking pomp and posturing."[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=First_Person_Shooter_\(song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

The song debuted at number one on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), becoming Drake's thirteenth and Cole's first number-one song on the chart, the former tying the record for most solo number-one songs by a solo male artist with [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson").[\[13\]](#cite_note-BBrecord-13) In its second week, the song remained in the top ten in the US _Billboard_ Hot 100 and fell to number eight.[\[14\]](#cite_note-BBrecord2-14) The song debuted at number-one on the _Billboard'_s Streaming Songs, marking Drake's 19th number-one on the chart.[\[14\]](#cite_note-BBrecord2-14)

In a first assessment of the album, Kyle Denis of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ ranked "First Person Shooter" as the ninth best track of the album, writing that the duo had adopted an "elder statesmen" mentality while still presenting their "skin in the game", but while their attitude was seen as "braggadocious", both were holding back a little.[\[3\]](#cite_note-billboard-3) _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_'s Mosi Reeves stated that on the song, Drake is "thoroughly outclassed by J Cole" and that his lyrics are basic, several of them being "desultory lyrics where he discusses women like he’s stocking a meat freezer."[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) Writing for _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_\(magazine\) "Clash (magazine)")_, Shahzaib Hussain notes that "First Person Shooter" sees Drake "all shit-talking pomp and posturing."[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=First_Person_Shooter_\(song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

The song debuted at number one on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), becoming Drake's thirteenth and Cole's first number-one song on the chart, the former tying the record for most solo number-one songs by a solo male artist with [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson").[\[13\]](#cite_note-BBrecord-13) In its second week, the song remained in the top ten in the US _Billboard_ Hot 100 and fell to number eight.[\[14\]](#cite_note-BBrecord2-14) The song debuted at number-one on the _Billboard'_s Streaming Songs, marking Drake's 19th number-one on the chart.[\[14\]](#cite_note-BBrecord2-14)

"**Slime You Out**" is a song by Canadian rapper [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") featuring American singer-songwriter [SZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SZA "SZA"). It was released through [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") as the lead single from Drake's eighth studio album, _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_, on September 15, 2023 to mixed reviews. The [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") song was produced by Drake himself and Noel Cadastre and co-produced by [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40_\(record_producer\) "40 (record producer)"), [Bnyx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bnyx "Bnyx"), and Dalton Tennant, and written by the five alongside SZA, Chris Powell, and Grant Lapointe, due to the song sampling "Just Ask Me" by the Soul Superbs. It debuted at number one on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), becoming Drake's twelfth and SZA's second number-one single on the chart.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)

Both artists were first linked together in the lyrics of "[Mr. Right Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Right_Now "Mr. Right Now")" (2020), when Drake revealed that he had dated her back in 2008.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) SZA initially responded by unfollowing the rapper on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"). However, she later confirmed that they indeed dated back in 2009 and that it was "all love all peace". In December 2022, she once again confirmed that they have had always been "cool" with each other.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)

On September 14, 2023, Drake and SZA shared a single cover of [Halle Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halle_Berry "Halle Berry") covered in [slime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunge "Gunge") at the [2012 Kids' Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Kids'_Choice_Awards "2012 Kids' Choice Awards") on their social media,[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) alluding to a collaboration.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) However, the posts did not contain any further information besides the artists tagging each other.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) Berry voiced out her disappointment in Drake on Instagram, stating that when she was asked by the rapper's team to give him permission to use her picture as a single cover, she refused.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) The single was eventually announced on September 15, without the cover.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

"Slime You Out" received mainly mixed reviews from critics, with SZA's feature receiving praise and the lyrics receiving criticism.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

_[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Kyle Denis ranks the track at #15 out of the 23 songs on Drake's _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_.[\[11\]](#cite_note-billboard-11) In his review of the song, he stated that the track is "far from the worst offering on _For All the Dogs_." He noted that "there are at least some real stakes and tension," however, "it’s still miles away from the surefire stunner that a SZA-Drake duet should be, but it’s not a complete waste of space."[\[11\]](#cite_note-billboard-11)

American radio host [Charlamagne tha God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlamagne_tha_God "Charlamagne tha God") said on his podcast “Drake put out a song last Friday and nobody cared” as well as “Well, it's Drake and SZA. People’s curiosity is going to make them go stream the record and of course, radio is going to play the hell out of it.”[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-:0-13) Drake responded calling Charlamagne an “off brand [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut")”.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) Charlamagne later joked his hate for the song was planned after it hit number one “I told y’all yesterday that Drake and I plan these things every time he drops certain records. He wants me to hate on them because all noise is great noise nowadays. And I told y’all the play but nobody believes me ’cause I'm lying. But you should believe me even when I'm lying.” [\[13\]](#cite_note-:0-13)

Fans also had problems with the lyrics, accusing the singer of "treating women like slaves".[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

"**Slime You Out**" is a song by Canadian rapper [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") featuring American singer-songwriter [SZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SZA "SZA"). It was released through [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") as the lead single from Drake's eighth studio album, _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_, on September 15, 2023 to mixed reviews. The [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") song was produced by Drake himself and Noel Cadastre and co-produced by [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40_\(record_producer\) "40 (record producer)"), [Bnyx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bnyx "Bnyx"), and Dalton Tennant, and written by the five alongside SZA, Chris Powell, and Grant Lapointe, due to the song sampling "Just Ask Me" by the Soul Superbs. It debuted at number one on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), becoming Drake's twelfth and SZA's second number-one single on the chart.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)

Both artists were first linked together in the lyrics of "[Mr. Right Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Right_Now "Mr. Right Now")" (2020), when Drake revealed that he had dated her back in 2008.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) SZA initially responded by unfollowing the rapper on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"). However, she later confirmed that they indeed dated back in 2009 and that it was "all love all peace". In December 2022, she once again confirmed that they have had always been "cool" with each other.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)

On September 14, 2023, Drake and SZA shared a single cover of [Halle Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halle_Berry "Halle Berry") covered in [slime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunge "Gunge") at the [2012 Kids' Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Kids'_Choice_Awards "2012 Kids' Choice Awards") on their social media,[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) alluding to a collaboration.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) However, the posts did not contain any further information besides the artists tagging each other.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) Berry voiced out her disappointment in Drake on Instagram, stating that when she was asked by the rapper's team to give him permission to use her picture as a single cover, she refused.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) The single was eventually announced on September 15, without the cover.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

"Slime You Out" received mainly mixed reviews from critics, with SZA's feature receiving praise and the lyrics receiving criticism.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

_[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s Kyle Denis ranks the track at #15 out of the 23 songs on Drake's _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_.[\[11\]](#cite_note-billboard-11) In his review of the song, he stated that the track is "far from the worst offering on _For All the Dogs_." He noted that "there are at least some real stakes and tension," however, "it’s still miles away from the surefire stunner that a SZA-Drake duet should be, but it’s not a complete waste of space."[\[11\]](#cite_note-billboard-11)

American radio host [Charlamagne tha God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlamagne_tha_God "Charlamagne tha God") said on his podcast “Drake put out a song last Friday and nobody cared” as well as “Well, it's Drake and SZA. People’s curiosity is going to make them go stream the record and of course, radio is going to play the hell out of it.”[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-:0-13) Drake responded calling Charlamagne an “off brand [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut")”.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) Charlamagne later joked his hate for the song was planned after it hit number one “I told y’all yesterday that Drake and I plan these things every time he drops certain records. He wants me to hate on them because all noise is great noise nowadays. And I told y’all the play but nobody believes me ’cause I'm lying. But you should believe me even when I'm lying.” [\[13\]](#cite_note-:0-13)

Fans also had problems with the lyrics, accusing the singer of "treating women like slaves".[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

"**Rich Baby Daddy**" is a song by Canadian rapper [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") featuring American rapper [Sexyy Red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexyy_Red "Sexyy Red") and American singer-songwriter [SZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SZA "SZA"). It was sent to Italian [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio") through [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") as the third single from Drake's eighth studio album, _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_, on October 13, 2023. The three artists wrote the song with producers [Gordo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordo_\(DJ_/_producer\) "Gordo (DJ / producer)"), Liohn, and Klahr, and co-producers [Bnyx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bnyx "Bnyx"), Dougie F, the Loud Pack, and UV Killin Em, alongside [Florence Welch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_Welch "Florence Welch"), [Isabella Summers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabella_Summers "Isabella Summers"), and T. Schaeferdieck, due to the song interpolating "[Dog Days Are Over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_Days_Are_Over "Dog Days Are Over")" by [Florence + the Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_and_the_Machine "Florence and the Machine"). While the song marks the first time that Sexyy Red has collaborated with both Drake and SZA, the latter two previously collaborated on "[Slime You Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slime_You_Out "Slime You Out")", which served as the lead single from _For All the Dogs_.

Writing for _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_, Mosi Reeves compared Drake matching his vocal performance to that of Sexyy Red on "Rich Baby Daddy" to him matching that of [City Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Girls "City Girls") on his 2018 single, "[In My Feelings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Feelings "In My Feelings")" and praised the sample of "[Dog Days Are Over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_Days_Are_Over "Dog Days Are Over")" by [Florence + the Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_and_the_Machine "Florence and the Machine").[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")'_s Dylan Green found Sexyy Red and SZA to be "two of the most memorable features" on _For All the Dogs_ and felt that their "raucous" parts on the song "live up to the song’s hectic, club-ready beat".[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) Kyle Denis of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ saw the song as "with infectious production that heavily nods to [Miami bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_bass "Miami bass"), this is the song of the summer that we deserved — from Sexyy's 'Looking for the Hoes' interpolation to an outro from Drake that basically cements him as the ultimate rich baby daddy" and saw it to be the potential "Song of the Fall".[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) Chris Richards at _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_ criticized the "stray" line "Take care of the dog until the dog days are over" that Drake rapped and called it an "inelegant hint at potentially forthcoming Drake redemption album".[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

An official music video was filmed during [New Year's Eve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Year's_Eve "New Year's Eve"), as well as February 4, 2024, which is when Sexyy Red gave birth unexpectedly during filming. The video was later officially released on February 14, 2024. It was directed by [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") himself.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) The video documents the actual birth of Sexyy Red's second child, including her transportation to the hospital after her water broke, as well as audio of her pushing the baby out. The video ends with Sexyy Red dancing in the hospital along with several other girls while holding her newly born child, who later gets held by SZA in another scene.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

SZA performed "Rich Baby Daddy" during the [Grand National Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_National_Tour "Grand National Tour") (2025), which she co-headlined with rapper [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar"). Prior to the tour, he and Drake were engaged in a highly publicized feud; its inclusion led Joe Lynch of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ to speculate on why it was performed: "Trolling? Tribute? Olive branch? Olive the above?"[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

While the song marks the first time that Sexyy Red has collaborated with both Drake and SZA, the latter two previously collaborated on "[Slime You Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slime_You_Out "Slime You Out")", which served as the lead single from _For All the Dogs_.

Writing for _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_, Mosi Reeves compared Drake matching his vocal performance to that of Sexyy Red on "Rich Baby Daddy" to him matching that of [City Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Girls "City Girls") on his 2018 single, "[In My Feelings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Feelings "In My Feelings")" and praised the sample of "[Dog Days Are Over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_Days_Are_Over "Dog Days Are Over")" by [Florence + the Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_and_the_Machine "Florence and the Machine").[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")'_s Dylan Green found Sexyy Red and SZA to be "two of the most memorable features" on _For All the Dogs_ and felt that their "raucous" parts on the song "live up to the song’s hectic, club-ready beat".[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) Kyle Denis of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ saw the song as "with infectious production that heavily nods to [Miami bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_bass "Miami bass"), this is the song of the summer that we deserved — from Sexyy's 'Looking for the Hoes' interpolation to an outro from Drake that basically cements him as the ultimate rich baby daddy" and saw it to be the potential "Song of the Fall".[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) Chris Richards at _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_ criticized the "stray" line "Take care of the dog until the dog days are over" that Drake rapped and called it an "inelegant hint at potentially forthcoming Drake redemption album".[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

An official music video was filmed during [New Year's Eve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Year's_Eve "New Year's Eve"), as well as February 4, 2024, which is when Sexyy Red gave birth unexpectedly during filming. The video was later officially released on February 14, 2024. It was directed by [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") himself.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) The video documents the actual birth of Sexyy Red's second child, including her transportation to the hospital after her water broke, as well as audio of her pushing the baby out. The video ends with Sexyy Red dancing in the hospital along with several other girls while holding her newly born child, who later gets held by SZA in another scene.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

SZA performed "Rich Baby Daddy" during the [Grand National Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_National_Tour "Grand National Tour") (2025), which she co-headlined with rapper [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar"). Prior to the tour, he and Drake were engaged in a highly publicized feud; its inclusion led Joe Lynch of _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ to speculate on why it was performed: "Trolling? Its production was handled by frequent collaborators [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40_\(record_producer\) "40 (record producer)"), [Nineteen85](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen85 "Nineteen85"), [PartyNextDoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor "PartyNextDoor"), [OZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz_\(record_producer\) "Oz (record producer)"), and [Vinylz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinylz "Vinylz"), among others. [Lil Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Baby "Lil Baby"), [Lil Durk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Durk "Lil Durk"), [Giveon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giveon "Giveon"), [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z"), [Travis Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Scott "Travis Scott"), [Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_\(rapper\) "Future (rapper)"), [Young Thug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Thug "Young Thug"), [Yebba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yebba "Yebba"), [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage"), [Project Pat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Pat "Project Pat"), [Tems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tems "Tems"), [Ty Dolla Sign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Dolla_Sign "Ty Dolla Sign"), [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne"), [Rick Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Ross "Rick Ross"), and [Kid Cudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Cudi "Kid Cudi") appear as guest artists. It is the first part of what Drake described as a "trilogy" of albums, that also includes the follow-ups _[Honestly, Nevermind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honestly,_Nevermind "Honestly, Nevermind")_ and _[Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss "Her Loss")_ (both 2022).

Similar to Drake's previous releases, the album predominantly deals with his views on fame and success, particularly his dominance within the music industry, alongside [misplaced loyalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misplaced_loyalty "Misplaced loyalty"), tainted [romances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_\(love\) "Romance (love)"), [feuds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feud "Feud"), and [loneliness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loneliness "Loneliness"). Primarily a [hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music") record, a hazy atmosphere dominates the album's sound, which includes elements of [crunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crunk "Crunk") and [trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music "Trap music"). Several writers found aspects of the album to be reminiscent of _[Thank Me Later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank_Me_Later "Thank Me Later")_ (2010), _[Take Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_Care_\(album\) "Take Care (album)")_ (2011) and _[Nothing Was the Same](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nothing_Was_the_Same "Nothing Was the Same")_ (2013). _Certified Lover Boy_ was dedicated to the late models Nadia Ntuli and Miss Mercedes Morr.[\[12\]](#cite_note-Cowen-12) Ntuli, who was a close friend of Drake's, was killed in a motor vehicle accident in Dubai in early 2021.[\[12\]](#cite_note-Cowen-12) Morr, born Janae Gagnier, was found dead in her Texas apartment on August 29, 2021. She was believed to be the victim of a [murder–suicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder–suicide "Murder–suicide").[\[12\]](#cite_note-Cowen-12) On November 26, 2022, Drake revealed that the album is part of a trilogy of albums with _[Honestly, Nevermind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honestly,_Nevermind "Honestly, Nevermind")_ and _[Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss "Her Loss")_.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

_**Her Loss**_ is a collaborative album by rappers [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") and [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage"). It was released on November 4, 2022, through [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") and [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"). The album features a sole guest appearance from [Travis Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Scott "Travis Scott"). Production was handled by a range of record producers, including [Boi-1da](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boi-1da "Boi-1da"), [Metro Boomin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Boomin "Metro Boomin"), [Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz_\(record_producer\) "Oz (record producer)"), [Tay Keith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tay_Keith "Tay Keith"), [Vinylz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinylz "Vinylz"), [Wheezy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheezy "Wheezy"), [Taz Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taz_Taylor_\(record_producer\) "Taz Taylor (record producer)"), and [Lil Yachty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Yachty "Lil Yachty"), among others. It is the final installment of what Drake described as a "trilogy", following _[Certified Lover Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy "Certified Lover Boy")_ (2021) and _[Honestly, Nevermind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honestly,_Nevermind "Honestly, Nevermind")_ (2022).

Drake and 21 Savage have frequently collaborated since 2016, with _Her Loss_ announced in the music video for their then-most recent collaboration "[Jimmy Cooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Cooks "Jimmy Cooks")". During marketing, Drake and 21 Savage spoofed music promotion techniques, including a _[Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vogue_\(magazine\) "Vogue (magazine)")_ cover, [Cartier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartier_\(jeweler\) "Cartier (jeweler)") advertisement, [Tiny Desk Concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tiny_Desk_Concerts "List of Tiny Desk Concerts"), interview on _[The Howard Stern Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Howard_Stern_Show "The Howard Stern Show")_, and televised and online live performances on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_ and [ColorsxStudios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ColorsxStudios "ColorsxStudios"): the artists settled after being sued by [Condé Nast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condé_Nast "Condé Nast") for using _Vogue_ trademarks without permission. Originally set for release on October 28, 2022, _Her Loss_ was delayed to November 4.

The album received mixed reviews from critics, with praise for its [fan service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fan_service "Fan service") but criticism for some of its lyrics, which [garnered controversy](#Controversy). _Her Loss_ opened with first-week sales of 404,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") in the United States and topped the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Billboard_200 "U.S. Billboard 200"), supported by the singles "[Rich Flex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Flex "Rich Flex")", "[Circo Loco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circo_Loco "Circo Loco")", and "[Spin Bout U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_Bout_U "Spin Bout U")". It was nominated for [Best Rap Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Album "Best Rap Album") at the [66th Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Grammy_Awards "66th Grammy Awards").

_Her Loss_ came after the duo's previous collaborations on "[Sneakin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sneakin' "Sneakin'")" (2016),[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) "Issa" (2017),[\[3\]](#cite_note-Dandridge-Lemco_2017-3) "[Mr. Right Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Right_Now "Mr. Right Now")" (2020),[\[4\]](#cite_note-Bloom-4) and "[Knife Talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knife_Talk "Knife Talk")" (2021).[\[4\]](#cite_note-Bloom-4) On June 17, 2022, Drake released the song "[Jimmy Cooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Cooks "Jimmy Cooks")" featuring 21 Savage as the final track of his seventh studio album _[Honestly, Nevermind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honestly,_Nevermind "Honestly, Nevermind")_. Upon release, the song was the most successful track off the album and debuted at number one on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"),[\[5\]](#cite_note-complex-5) but the song was not officially serviced to mainstream radio as a single until October 11.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) On October 19, Drake performed as a surprise guest at one of 21 Savage's concerts in Atlanta.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

On October 21, Drake announced the "Jimmy Cooks" music video would be released on 21 Savage's 30th birthday a day later.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) The video was eventually released that day.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) The visuals were briefly interrupted at the 1:25-mark, with text in typographic letters appearing reading "Her Loss – album by Drake and 21 Savage – October 28, 2022".[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) The album was then confirmed by [OVO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") and [Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") on their social media.[\[5\]](#cite_note-complex-5)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) On October 26, Drake announced the album had been delayed to November 4, 2022, due to OVO record producer [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40_\(record_producer\) "40 (record producer)") contracting [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") during the album's mixing and mastering proces

Canadian-American professional basketball player [Tristan Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tristan_Thompson "Tristan Thompson") makes an appearance as his [best man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groomsman "Groomsman").[\[10\]](#cite_note-Fader-10)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

The album's only feature, [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage"), appears on the closing track of the album, "[Jimmy Cooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Cooks "Jimmy Cooks")".[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) The album's first two singles, "[Sticky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sticky_\(Drake_song\) "Sticky (Drake song)")" and "[Massive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massive_\(song\) "Massive (song)")" were sent to [rhythmic contemporary radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") and [contemporary hit radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_hit_radio "Contemporary hit radio"), respectively, on June 21.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) "Jimmy Cooks" impacted contemporary hit radio on October 11, as the album's third single.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) On November 26, 2022, Drake revealed that the album is part of a trilogy of albums following _Certified Lover Boy_ and later _[Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss "Her Loss")_.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

# Did Quentin Miller write lyrics for Drake’s songs? Details explored as clips surface of ghostwriter explaining his writing relationship with Drizzy

![close](//staticg.sportskeeda.com/cmc-predictor/v2/cross-icon.png?w=40)

Quentin Miller is an Atlanta rapper who is well known for being credited as a writer and for ghostwriting songs for other popular artists. Miller has repped his OVO connections through social media, posting OVO Ryan and PARTYNEXTDOOR quite often, identifying himself as a part of Drake's exclusive social circle.

Miller has also worked and is credited on some of Drizzy's projects, including the 2015 Grammy-nominated album _If You're Reading This It's Too Late_. Soon after the album release, the Drake vs. Meek Mill beef became a main point of discussion on the internet. It began on July 21, 2015, after Meek tweeted that the OVO CEO used ghostwriters for his songs. Although the tweet has since been deleted, it can still be found on multiple websites, including Genius.com

> "Stop comparing drake to me too... He don't write his own raps! That's why he aint tweet out my album because we found out," Meek Mill's tweet read.

Expand Tweet

Drizzy responded to Meek's ghostwriting allegations and dropped _Back To Back,_ following which he appeared to have commercially distanced himself from Miller. The ATL rapper was outed as Drake's "Ghostwriter" after Mill allegedly had the demo of Miller's recording on _10 Bands_ and other reference tracks leak online.

Over the last few days, clips from Quentin Miller's 2022 interview with DJ Vlad resurfaced on X. These show him recapping stories of working on music with Drake and diving into his contribution to _If You're Reading This It's Too Late._ In the interview, he also discussed his involvement in the 2015 rap beef and more.

* * *

## Highlights from Quentin Miller's interview with DJ Vlad

In 2022, Quentin sat down for an [exclusive interview](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/kanye-west-sits-exclusive-interview-justin-laboy-discuss-like-that-remix-drake) with DJ Vlad. He discussed several topics, including a specific discussion around his relationship with Drake. This article will take a look at the top moments where Quentin Miller discussed Drake and his experience working with the Canadian rapper.

![youtube-cover](https://staticg.sportskeeda.com/editor/2024/05/34ab0-17169908765014-1920.jpg)

* * *

### 1) Working on _If You're Reading This It's Too Late_

Miller told DJ Vlad why he appreciated his time working on _If You're Reading This It's Too Late._ He recapped memories of sending ideas to Drake and his team, writing over 5 songs for [the album](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/breaking-down-apple-music-s-best-album-time-the-miseducation-lauryn-hill), and meeting Drizzy for the first time.

DJ Vlad asked Quentin Miller to explain the difference between working with Drake and other popular artists. Quentin said that he was surprised at how "regular it felt."

> "To me it was surprising just how, like, regular it felt. It felt like making a song with friends. Just going back n forth, jus bouncin'... it was real down to earth vibes, in the studio, you know," Miller noted.

* * *

### 2) Co-writing Drake's verse for Meek Mill's _R.I.C.O_

![Quentin Miller from his interview with DJ Vlad (Image via YouTube/@vladtv)](https://staticg.sportskeeda.com/editor/2024/05/b5737-17170008144261-1920.jpg?w=640)

Quentin Miller from his interview with DJ Vlad (Image via YouTube/@vladtv)

A few months before Drake and Meek started publicly beefing, [the two rappers](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/a-list-10-popular-rappers-currently-serving-time-jail-prison) featured together on Mill's 2015 album _Dreams Worth More Than Money_. DJ Vlad brought up the song and asked Quentin to break down his involvement in the song.

As per Miller, the only people who were aware of his ghostwriting work were DJ Drama and Drake, as they had received his demo for _R.I.C.O._ Following this, DJ Drama supposedly sent [the track](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/breaking-drake-s-fourth-diss-track-the-heart-part-6) to Meek Mill, who had Drake feature on it, without Quentin being involved.

The writer-rapper then went on to discuss how he felt used in the Drake vs. Meek beef. He explained that Drama played a lot of Drake reference tracks with Quentin Miller's vocals in front of Nicki Minaj and [Meek Mill](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/news-bro-got-tired-allegations-internet-reacts-meek-mill-unfollows-diddy-amid-cassie-controversy). This event is what is claimed to have led to Meek Mill's 2015 tweet about Drizzy working with ghostwriters.

* * *

### 3) Getting caught up in the middle of the Meek Mill vs Drake beef

Quentin Miller then explained the reality of being drawn into a rap beef between two major rappers. He went on to explain how Meek used him as an example to put down the [Canadian rapper](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/20-savage-bars-kendrick-lamar-drake-s-diss-tracks)'s creative talent, which tarnished Miller's professional relationship with Drake.

He expressed how being outed as a ghostwriter led to [many artists](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/weekly-music-radar-guide-biggest-releases-week-b662785a) distancing themselves from Miller and his work. Quentin also spoke about how he felt OVO 40 and Drake should have dealt with this situation. He noted that they diminished him to control the situation, instead of uplifting him.

> "One thing that I don't like that \[OVO 40 and Drake\] did man, you know, in hindsight... They felt like they had to diminish me to keep the situation... Why you s--tting on me, you could easily uplift me. I see bro uplift all kinds of artists. It just put me in a bad situation, it put a bad taste in people's mouth for me, especially in the industry," Quentin said.

* * *

### 4) Quentin explains how he never got paid for any of his work with Drake

![Quentin Miller from his interview with DJ Vlad (Image via YouTube/@vladtv)](https://staticg.sportskeeda.com/editor/2024/05/603da-17170008300896-1920.jpg?w=640)

Quentin Miller from his interview with DJ Vlad (Image via YouTube/@vladtv)

Quentin Miller explained that signing a $30,000 publishing deal with Grammy-winning producer Tricky Steward affected his career as an artist the most. He claimed that, although the deal was really bad and he was unable to make ends meet, linking up with Drake appeared to be a major moment in his career.

Miller didn't break down the exact details of his publishing deal, but he noted that he holds a grudge for the way he was treated under the agreement that had him tied down for almost a decade.

He explained the difficulty of living under the repercussions of the Drake vs. Meek Mill beef and still being signed under Tricky's publishing deal.

> "By the time it all blew up, I hadn't worked out whatever situation could have been worked out to where my life would have been changed, by the time it all blew up and Drake wasn't f--king with me no more, Drama wasn't f--king with me no more, and I still was in that publishing deal," Quentin Miller stated during the interview.

* * *

Consistent claims have been made over the years about Drake using ghostwriters, especially since the Quentin Miller x Meek Mill beef. However, the claims were heavily referenced this year during [Drizzy's beef with Kendrick Lamar](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/drake-kendrick-diss-tracks-order-chronology-complete-list). K-Dot spent over four dedicated diss tracks claiming people in OVO and within Drake's circle helped him write on his records.
