# Did Quentin Miller write lyrics for Drake’s songs? Details explored as clips surface of ghostwriter explaining his writing relationship with Drizzy

![close](//staticg.sportskeeda.com/cmc-predictor/v2/cross-icon.png?w=40)

Quentin Miller is an Atlanta rapper who is well known for being credited as a writer and for ghostwriting songs for other popular artists. Miller has repped his OVO connections through social media, posting OVO Ryan and PARTYNEXTDOOR quite often, identifying himself as a part of Drake's exclusive social circle.

Miller has also worked and is credited on some of Drizzy's projects, including the 2015 Grammy-nominated album _If You're Reading This It's Too Late_. Soon after the album release, the Drake vs. Meek Mill beef became a main point of discussion on the internet. It began on July 21, 2015, after Meek tweeted that the OVO CEO used ghostwriters for his songs. Although the tweet has since been deleted, it can still be found on multiple websites, including Genius.com

> "Stop comparing drake to me too... He don't write his own raps! That's why he aint tweet out my album because we found out," Meek Mill's tweet read.

Expand Tweet

Drizzy responded to Meek's ghostwriting allegations and dropped _Back To Back,_ following which he appeared to have commercially distanced himself from Miller. The ATL rapper was outed as Drake's "Ghostwriter" after Mill allegedly had the demo of Miller's recording on _10 Bands_ and other reference tracks leak online.

Over the last few days, clips from Quentin Miller's 2022 interview with DJ Vlad resurfaced on X. These show him recapping stories of working on music with Drake and diving into his contribution to _If You're Reading This It's Too Late._ In the interview, he also discussed his involvement in the 2015 rap beef and more.

* * *

## Highlights from Quentin Miller's interview with DJ Vlad

In 2022, Quentin sat down for an [exclusive interview](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/kanye-west-sits-exclusive-interview-justin-laboy-discuss-like-that-remix-drake) with DJ Vlad. He discussed several topics, including a specific discussion around his relationship with Drake. This article will take a look at the top moments where Quentin Miller discussed Drake and his experience working with the Canadian rapper.

![youtube-cover](https://staticg.sportskeeda.com/editor/2024/05/34ab0-17169908765014-1920.jpg)

* * *

### 1) Working on _If You're Reading This It's Too Late_

Miller told DJ Vlad why he appreciated his time working on _If You're Reading This It's Too Late._ He recapped memories of sending ideas to Drake and his team, writing over 5 songs for [the album](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/breaking-down-apple-music-s-best-album-time-the-miseducation-lauryn-hill), and meeting Drizzy for the first time.

DJ Vlad asked Quentin Miller to explain the difference between working with Drake and other popular artists. Quentin said that he was surprised at how "regular it felt."

> "To me it was surprising just how, like, regular it felt. It felt like making a song with friends. Just going back n forth, jus bouncin'... it was real down to earth vibes, in the studio, you know," Miller noted.

* * *

### 2) Co-writing Drake's verse for Meek Mill's _R.I.C.O_

![Quentin Miller from his interview with DJ Vlad (Image via YouTube/@vladtv)](https://staticg.sportskeeda.com/editor/2024/05/b5737-17170008144261-1920.jpg?w=640)

Quentin Miller from his interview with DJ Vlad (Image via YouTube/@vladtv)

A few months before Drake and Meek started publicly beefing, [the two rappers](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/a-list-10-popular-rappers-currently-serving-time-jail-prison) featured together on Mill's 2015 album _Dreams Worth More Than Money_. DJ Vlad brought up the song and asked Quentin to break down his involvement in the song.

As per Miller, the only people who were aware of his ghostwriting work were DJ Drama and Drake, as they had received his demo for _R.I.C.O._ Following this, DJ Drama supposedly sent [the track](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/breaking-drake-s-fourth-diss-track-the-heart-part-6) to Meek Mill, who had Drake feature on it, without Quentin being involved.

The writer-rapper then went on to discuss how he felt used in the Drake vs. Meek beef. He explained that Drama played a lot of Drake reference tracks with Quentin Miller's vocals in front of Nicki Minaj and [Meek Mill](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/news-bro-got-tired-allegations-internet-reacts-meek-mill-unfollows-diddy-amid-cassie-controversy). This event is what is claimed to have led to Meek Mill's 2015 tweet about Drizzy working with ghostwriters.

* * *

### 3) Getting caught up in the middle of the Meek Mill vs Drake beef

Quentin Miller then explained the reality of being drawn into a rap beef between two major rappers. He went on to explain how Meek used him as an example to put down the [Canadian rapper](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/20-savage-bars-kendrick-lamar-drake-s-diss-tracks)'s creative talent, which tarnished Miller's professional relationship with Drake.

He expressed how being outed as a ghostwriter led to [many artists](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/weekly-music-radar-guide-biggest-releases-week-b662785a) distancing themselves from Miller and his work. Quentin also spoke about how he felt OVO 40 and Drake should have dealt with this situation. He noted that they diminished him to control the situation, instead of uplifting him.

> "One thing that I don't like that \[OVO 40 and Drake\] did man, you know, in hindsight... They felt like they had to diminish me to keep the situation... Why you s--tting on me, you could easily uplift me. I see bro uplift all kinds of artists. It just put me in a bad situation, it put a bad taste in people's mouth for me, especially in the industry," Quentin said.

* * *

### 4) Quentin explains how he never got paid for any of his work with Drake

![Quentin Miller from his interview with DJ Vlad (Image via YouTube/@vladtv)](https://staticg.sportskeeda.com/editor/2024/05/603da-17170008300896-1920.jpg?w=640)

Quentin Miller from his interview with DJ Vlad (Image via YouTube/@vladtv)

Quentin Miller explained that signing a $30,000 publishing deal with Grammy-winning producer Tricky Steward affected his career as an artist the most. He claimed that, although the deal was really bad and he was unable to make ends meet, linking up with Drake appeared to be a major moment in his career.

Miller didn't break down the exact details of his publishing deal, but he noted that he holds a grudge for the way he was treated under the agreement that had him tied down for almost a decade.

He explained the difficulty of living under the repercussions of the Drake vs. Meek Mill beef and still being signed under Tricky's publishing deal.

> "By the time it all blew up, I hadn't worked out whatever situation could have been worked out to where my life would have been changed, by the time it all blew up and Drake wasn't f--king with me no more, Drama wasn't f--king with me no more, and I still was in that publishing deal," Quentin Miller stated during the interview.

* * *

Consistent claims have been made over the years about Drake using ghostwriters, especially since the Quentin Miller x Meek Mill beef. However, the claims were heavily referenced this year during [Drizzy's beef with Kendrick Lamar](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/drake-kendrick-diss-tracks-order-chronology-complete-list). K-Dot spent over four dedicated diss tracks claiming people in OVO and within Drake's circle helped him write on his records.

_**Let’s go to [Take Care](https://tidal.com/browse/album/14234315). I remember \[the last time\] we talked…you were candid about what you liked and didn’t like about your first album...you’d begun recording, and you did some stuff with [9th Wonder](https://twitter.com/9thwonder?lang=en) and [Q-Tip](https://twitter.com/QtipTheAbstract?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Eauthor), but...it seemed by the time you got into the heart of 2011’s Take Care, it went to a whole other place. Like,**_ **Fuck it, this is my lane, nobody does it like me, I’m going to deliver.** _**Am I accurate?**_

Yeah…I’m human. I often get baited into hip-hop debates. And I often feel that I don’t get enough credit as a bar-for-bar MC because of the fact that I choose to take musical risks. And I also feel like when other people take musical risks, they get...more credit than me. With that being said, I found myself, and my sound when I went back home. _Take Care_, much like _[So Far Gone](https://tidal.com/browse/album/104161474)_, sounds like our city. If you spend six months there, and get to know the people, and you find yourself a girl there, and you end up going out there — it really sounds like our city...And — not to say that every project I do is going to be like that...But yeah, at first I guess I was trying to be like _Oh, I’m gonna make the rapper’s rap album, and I’m just gonna rap, and I’m gonna prove that I’m one of the best._ And then I realized, like, _You know what? Fuck you._ Like, I can prove that I’m one of the best without…without the names. The names don’t mean anything. If the songs aren’t good, they’re not good. If me and so-and-so don’t make a bunch of music like me and [40](https://youtu.be/JPEZnV2Lepc) would, or me and [Jamie xx](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/jamie-xx-new-song-idontknow-984278/) would…that moves people, that I can come to Berlin and do for 8,000-9,000 people, or go do 30,000 people in London…if it’s not going to work, then what’s the point? # Quentin Miller Is Actually Not Credited on "R.I.C.O."

In the couple weeks since [**Meek Mill** accused **Drake** of employing a ghostwriter, **Quentin Miller**,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/jay-balfour/meek-mill-says-drake-dont-write-his-own-raps) to write the Toronto superstar's rap verses, Miller and OVO producer **Noah "40" Shebib** have [publicly insisted that Miller is a co-writer, not a ghostwriter,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/jay-balfour/noah-40-shebib-weighs-in-on-drake-ghostwriting-contoversy) since Miller is officially credited for his songwriting contributions in the liner notes of Drake's _If You're Reading This It's Too Late_. In a Tumblr post dated July 24, [Miller claimed, "I am not and never will be a 'ghostwriter' for drake."](https://www.complex.com/music/a/zach-frydenlund/quentin-miller-speaks-about-drake-ghostwriting-rumors)

Much of the news coverage that's advanced this narrative cites Genius and Wikipedia as corroboration of Miller and 40's claims. Both Genius and Wikipedia are user-edited platforms, however, and are not official, definitive sources of information. The inattention to actual liner notes of [Meek Mill's _Dreams Worth More Than Money_,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/david-drake/meek-mill-dreams-worth-more-than-money-review) published by Atlantic Records, has sowed popular confusion regarding [Quentin Miller's involvement in Drake's songwriting.](https://www.complex.com/music/a/frazier-tharpe/quentin-miller-drake-ghostwriter)

In the interest of clarification, below is a screenshot of the official liner notes that are included in the physical CD release of Meek Mill's _Dreams Worth More Than Money_. Despite having laid [a reference track for Drake's verse on Meek's "R.I.C.O."](https://youtu.be/cdp0-ceqenM)—over the very same beat, no less—Quentin Miller is not credited for a co-writing contribution to the song. This evidence suggests that the description of Quentin Miller as a "ghostwriter" is, indeed, accurate, despite OVO's claims to the contrary. It also seems to corroborate Meek's claim that he was misled regarding the authorship of Drake's verse on "R.I.C.O."

It's now unclear whether Quentin Miller has written other Drake verses for which he is uncredited.

We've yet to learn why, after years of friendship and collaboration, Meek Mill suddenly decided to expose Drake's use of ghostwriters. Even in a field as competitive as hip-hop, [and even with a deformed love triangle at the heart of the matter,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/claire-lobenfeld/drake-leave-nicki-out-of-this) it's tough to believe that this specific, incendiary claim is one that Meek would've just tossed out in the heat of the moment.

Drake has so far managed to suffocate Meek Mill's ghostwriting claims with [a series of diss records,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/zach-frydenlund/drake-meek-mill-instagram-response)[Instagram captions,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/zach-frydenlund/drake-meek-mill-instagram-response)[interview quotes,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/eric-diep/drake-lebron-james-kick-ball-game) and [OVO festival promotion.](https://www.complex.com/music/a/olga/new-drake-track-ovo-fest) Still, Drake hasn't really answered Meek's initial complaint on its own merits. He appears to be ducking the fade.

_Additional reporting from Brandon Jenkins and Insanul Ahmed._

In the couple weeks since [**Meek Mill** accused **Drake** of employing a ghostwriter, **Quentin Miller**,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/jay-balfour/meek-mill-says-drake-dont-write-his-own-raps) to write the Toronto superstar's rap verses, Miller and OVO producer **Noah "40" Shebib** have [publicly insisted that Miller is a co-writer, not a ghostwriter,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/jay-balfour/noah-40-shebib-weighs-in-on-drake-ghostwriting-contoversy) since Miller is officially credited for his songwriting contributions in the liner notes of Drake's _If You're Reading This It's Too Late_. In a Tumblr post dated July 24, [Miller claimed, "I am not and never will be a 'ghostwriter' for drake."](https://www.complex.com/music/a/zach-frydenlund/quentin-miller-speaks-about-drake-ghostwriting-rumors)

Much of the news coverage that's advanced this narrative cites Genius and Wikipedia as corroboration of Miller and 40's claims. Both Genius and Wikipedia are user-edited platforms, however, and are not official, definitive sources of information. The inattention to actual liner notes of [Meek Mill's _Dreams Worth More Than Money_,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/david-drake/meek-mill-dreams-worth-more-than-money-review) published by Atlantic Records, has sowed popular confusion regarding [Quentin Miller's involvement in Drake's songwriting.](https://www.complex.com/music/a/frazier-tharpe/quentin-miller-drake-ghostwriter)

In the interest of clarification, below is a screenshot of the official liner notes that are included in the physical CD release of Meek Mill's _Dreams Worth More Than Money_. Despite having laid [a reference track for Drake's verse on Meek's "R.I.C.O."](https://youtu.be/cdp0-ceqenM)—over the very same beat, no less—Quentin Miller is not credited for a co-writing contribution to the song. This evidence suggests that the description of Quentin Miller as a "ghostwriter" is, indeed, accurate, despite OVO's claims to the contrary. It also seems to corroborate Meek's claim that he was misled regarding the authorship of Drake's verse on "R.I.C.O."

It's now unclear whether Quentin Miller has written other Drake verses for which he is uncredited.

We've yet to learn why, after years of friendship and collaboration, Meek Mill suddenly decided to expose Drake's use of ghostwriters. Even in a field as competitive as hip-hop, [and even with a deformed love triangle at the heart of the matter,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/claire-lobenfeld/drake-leave-nicki-out-of-this) it's tough to believe that this specific, incendiary claim is one that Meek would've just tossed out in the heat of the moment.

Drake has so far managed to suffocate Meek Mill's ghostwriting claims with [a series of diss records,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/zach-frydenlund/drake-meek-mill-instagram-response)[Instagram captions,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/zach-frydenlund/drake-meek-mill-instagram-response)[interview quotes,](https://www.complex.com/music/a/eric-diep/drake-lebron-james-kick-ball-game) and [OVO festival promotion.](https://www.complex.com/music/a/olga/new-drake-track-ovo-fest) Still, Drake hasn't really answered Meek's initial complaint on its own merits. He appears to be ducking the fade.

_Additional reporting from Brandon Jenkins and Insanul Ahmed._

Shebib, who has worked alongside Drake for the better part of a decade, shared a series of Tweets tonight confirming that he's worked in the studio with Miller but also came to Drake's defense, saying, "No one is as talented as Drake." Shebib also wrote that after approximately 5,000 hours in the studio with Drake he's only been in the studio together with Miller for less than an hour.

# Outtakes: Drake Talks Beyoncé, ‘Trophies’ And Next Album In VIBE Interview

![Drake talks Beyonce's "Mine"](https://www.vibe.com/wp-content/uploads/photo_gallery_images/outtakes-drake-vibe-cover-story.jpg?w=600&h=511&crop=1)

### What you won’t read in Drake’s second-ever VIBE cover story

**It’s nearly 1 a.m. on** a chilly November night and Charlotte’s Time Warner Cable Arena is dead. Two hours ago, the Bobcats’ stomping grounds was bustling as [Drake](https://www.vibe.com/t/drake/)’s Would You Like A Tour? concert sent thousands home reciting their favorite _[Nothing Was The Same](https://www.vibe.com/t/nothing-was-the-same/)_ tracks. But now, it’s just you and Toronto’s greatest rapper tucked away in a [Drakified team locker room](https://www.vibe.com/2013/12/vibe-winter-2014-cover-story-drake/) for the encore presentation: A first-listen of Drizzy’s new collaboration with [Beyoncé](https://www.vibe.com/t/beyonce/), “Mine,” which he finished recording last night.

He’ll allude to the the track a few times before finally pressing play on a song that’s definitely not Bey. From the two seconds that slip, it sounds like [Jet Life artist MaryGold, who makes a quick cameo at the end of his “Worst Behavior” video](https://www.vibe.com/2013/11/marygold-hip-hops-newest-obsession-12-things-you-should-know-about-currenys-jet-life/). Fingertips suddenly sweaty, you brace yourself as he reassesses his cluttered MacBook Pro desktop. And then it hits. Slow and somber, the opening stanza erupts from dancing piano keys to nimble percussion. He’ll narrate as the instrumental blooms. “Sampha’s on this, too,” he informs. When you mention that her lyrics have that signature Drake transparency he chuckles and offers a modest thanks.

“I had fun with it. I always wanted to write for her,” says the singing rapper, careful to embargo the then-untitled track from Bey’s hush-hush fifth solo LP. “She never really sings that minimal… We’ll see where that goes.”

Drake has been chatting for quite a bit longer than the scant 40 minutes allotted by his management for [this cover story](https://www.vibe.com/2013/12/vibe-winter-2014-cover-story-drake/), but he doesn’t seem to be in a rush. There’s none of the “Get the fuck up out my dressing room confusing me with questions” bitterness that he expresses on “HYFR.” He wants to deconstruct his new album as thoroughly as possible, while his security, managers, father and OVO fam members shoot the shit outside. He smiles big and often, punctuating and tenderizing his more confident or abrasive statements. We’ll go on some tangents, but after an hour-and-a-half interview there’s a bit more goodness than there are pages to print. From whether he’d ever record a concept LP to [Mase](https://www.vibe.com/t/mase/)’s resurgence to _NWTS_‘s follow-up, here’s the best of what was left on the cutting room floor. —_John Kennedy_

**VIBE: You start the song “Furthest Thing” with the line, “Somewhere between psychotic and iconic.” What does that place feel like?**  
**Drake:** It’s just forever hanging in the balance of knowing in the far-off distance there’s this vision of being as legendary as Hov, Pac, Bob Marley—who knows what the possibilities are? I’m not sure what I mean to this generation; I won’t understand until the story plays out. But there is that vision of the legacy. There’s also so many opportunities to plummet and not reach that. I keep pushing forward, but sometimes I glance back like, Damn, that shit’s crazy back there. Look at all those guys back there. That shit’s scary. That shit can drive you crazy. That’s what that line means to me. There are two directions you can go. It’s up to you.

**That song is one of a few where the beat evolves as you listen. That’s always been a musical theme for you, but it’s a bit more conspicuous here than in your prior works.**  
I gotta give the credit to 40. He wouldn’t just let a beat sit. I would leave the studio and by the time I came back the next day, he’d be like “I added some shit.” Even this Beyoncé record that we did (“Mine”). It’s kinda like ever-evolving, but I felt like we were working on an album and sitting on it for so long. We played \[songs\] for people and I started hearing that formula on other people’s stuff, too. That’s nothing to coin, to say we started that. But I think 40 does it the best out of everybody. He’s just been so amazing at making a piece grow or shrink, but it was all credit due to him for that. He was the mastermind behind the music.

**You experiment with different flows on this one, too. Was that a conscious thing?**

# Drake’s Songwriting Process Includes Pitching Tents in the Vocal Booth

As [Drake](//www.xxlmag.com/tags/drake/) pushes towards the finish line with _Views From the 6_, a bit of insight on the rapper's recording process has come to light thanks to OVO signees [Majid Jordan](//www.xxlmag.com/tags/majid-jordan/). While sitting down with Hot 97's _Ebro in the Morning_, the singers/songwriters/producers revealed that they came up with Drake's "Hold On We're Going Home," what would be the second single off his third studio album _Nothing Was the Same_, after camping out in the studio.

When asked if it was difficult relinquishing the rights to the song, the duo answered, "The song wasn’t something we just had ready and prepared and they heard. We got back to Toronto and they were just starting the beginnings of _Nothing was the Same_, in 2013. They basically put us in the studio and it was like a studio camp, almost, there were tents in there. There were people flying in there... There were tents in the studio. I slept in a tent in the studio."

The process sounds grueling, but for an up-and-coming act, it's likely worth it to collaborate with Drake and kickstart a career. With [the release of "Summer Sixteen,"](//www.xxlmag.com/rap-music/new-music/2016/01/drake-summer-sixteen/) Drake announced that _Views_ will be dropping sometime in April. In January, Drake's in-house producer Noah “40” Shebib [offered a hint as to the album's status](//www.xxlmag.com/news/2016/01/noah-40-shebib-hints-that-drakes-views-from-the-6-album-is-complete/), posting an image of a computer folder titled "Views" to Instagram.

As "Hotline Bling" continues to breathe new life, being featured in [an upcoming T-Mobile Super Bowl ad](//www.xxlmag.com/news/2016/02/drake-t-mobile-hotline-bling-super-bowl-ad/), there's little pressure for Drake to tip his hand or release anything other than promo tracks, what "Summer Sixteen" will likely add up to being. With the [NBA All Star Weekend in Toronto](//www.xxlmag.com/news/2016/02/drake-toronto-raptors-broadcast-nba-all-star-weekend/) coming up, there's always the chance that Drizzy drops a bombshell to get his city going. For the meantime though, fans will have to imagine OVO campfires and ghost stories, and the flames of some tent-inspired recording session.

**See 40 Hip-Hop Albums Turning 20 in 2016**

7. Low discard rate: "If I'm gonna go as far as to track over a beat I usually have the utmost faith in it... I don't really dispose of too many songs" (Drake 2013).
8. In-room testing: play it loud, watch the room (The Motto method).

# Research: Drake (Aubrey Drake Graham) — The "Drake Melody" Hit Formula

**Lane:** Drake (OVO Sound/Republic) — most Billboard Hot 100 entries in history; the genre-hopping melodic-rap-singing hit machine.

## Summary

Drake's repeatable method, documented across 15 years of interviews, is: **melody first, words second, recorded the same night the beat arrives, tested in the room, and shipped fast.** He works with a rotating army of producers (Boi-1da, Noah "40" Shebib, Gordo, Southside, PartyNextDoor, Bnyx, Tay Keith, Vinylz, OZ, Elkan…), who send him beats; he mostly ignores submissions until one hits, then he locks himself in and lays a hook + first verse in one sitting ("five songs in one night" — Gordo). Hooks are built on short, repeated, singable phrases over **minor-key** production ("40 produces in minor and I'll find the melodies to slip around it" — Drake), with emotion as the quality gate ("that it penetrates"). His words serve the melody — conversational, direct-address, low literary density — and his biggest 2020-2025 records ("Slime You Out", "First Person Shooter", "Rich Baby Daddy", "Nokia") all follow the same skeleton: a proven or sampled hook melody, a sparse beat that clears space for the vocal, and a fast release cadence that converts cultural moment into chart moment (7 No. 1s in 2020-2025; 13 career No. 1s through 2025).

---

## 1) Verified credentials & 2020-2025 relevance

**Chart records (Billboard, verified):**
- **Most career Hot 100 entries ever — 402** (as of the May 30, 2026 chart, per Billboard Canada's running ledger); he has held the record for the most Hot 100 visits since **early 2020**, was first to 300 entries (with *For All the Dogs*, 2023) and first to 400 (2026). [Billboard Canada records page](https://ca.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/drake-hot-100-records); [Billboard: first to 400](https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/drake-first-artist-400-hot-100-hits-1236256941/)
- **14 No. 1 Hot 100 hits** — the most among solo male artists (13 through end of 2025; 14th in 2026). Also records for most top-2 (27), top-3 (35), top-5 (47), top-10 (90), top-20 (154), top-40 (241) hits, and **10 No. 1 debuts** (most ever). Has peaked at 95 of the chart's 100 positions. [Billboard Canada records page](https://ca.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/drake-hot-100-records)
- 431 consecutive weeks on the Hot 100 (2009-2017) — all-time record. [Billboard Canada records page](https://ca.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/drake-hot-100-records)

**RIAA:**
- **Most diamond-certified songs of any artist ever** — 10th diamond plaque in May 2025, extended to **15 diamond-certified songs** with six new diamonds on his 39th birthday (Oct 2025: "Nice for What", "The Motto", "Headlines", "Passionfruit", "Nonstop", album *Take Care*). "Best I Ever Had" and "Hold On, We're Going Home" went diamond in 2025. [Billboard Oct 2025](https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/drake-diamond-riaa-39th-birthday-1236097599/); [Billboard May 2025](https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/drake-breaks-record-riaa-diamond-certifications-1235982872/); [RIAA database](https://www.riaa.com/gold-%20platinum/?se=drake&tab_active=default-award)

**2020-2025 releases (all Billboard 200 No. 1s):**
- *Dark Lane Demo Tapes* (May 2020); "Toosie Slide" (Apr 2020) — **No. 1 debut**, quarantine/TikTok dance single.
- *Scary Hours 2* (Mar 2021): "What's Next" **No. 1 debut**.
- *Certified Lover Boy* (Sept 3, 2021) — **613,000 first-week units**, biggest opening week of 2021, record 9 top-10s from one album; Drake held the entire Hot 100 top 5 (Sept 18, 2021 chart); "Way 2 Sexy" **No. 1** (his 9th). [Wikipedia/CLB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy); [Billboard Canada](https://ca.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/drake-hot-100-records)
- *Honestly, Nevermind* (June 17, 2022, surprise drop) — **204,000 units**; "Jimmy Cooks" **No. 1** (11th). [Wikipedia/HN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honestly,_Nevermind)
- *Her Loss* w/ 21 Savage (Nov 4, 2022) — **404,000 units**; 15 songs in the top 20 in week 2 (record); delayed one week because **40 caught COVID during mixing/mastering**. [Wikipedia/Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss)
- *For All the Dogs* (Oct 6, 2023) — **402,000 units**, 514M global streams in debut week (biggest streaming week of 2023); "Slime You Out" **No. 1** (12th) and "First Person Shooter" **No. 1** (13th, tying Michael Jackson for most No. 1s by a solo male). [Wikipedia/FATD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs); *Scary Hours 3* deluxe (Nov 2023).
- *100 Gigs: For Your Eyes Only* (Aug 2024); beef singles "Push Ups", "Taylor Made Freestyle", "Family Matters" (spring 2024).
- **$ome $exy $ongs 4 U** w/ PartyNextDoor (Feb 14, 2025) — **246,000 units**, Drake's 14th No. 1 album (ties Jay-Z & Taylor Swift for most among solo artists); "Nokia" peaked **No. 2** on the Hot 100 (April 19, 2025). [Wikipedia/SSS4U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Sexy_Songs_4_U); [Wikipedia/Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_(song))
- 2025 also: "Somebody Loves Me", "Die Trying" (singles), the Some Special Shows 4 U tour; Jan 2025 defamation lawsuit vs. UMG over "Not Like Us" (see §Controversy).

**Controversy context (no-taboos summary, full facts in §3/§7):** Quentin Miller/Meek Mill 2015 reference-track scandal; Pusha T's "Infrared" (2018); 2024 Kendrick Lamar feud ("Like That", "Euphoria", "6:16 in LA", "Meet the Grahams", "Not Like Us") that resurfaced the ghostwriting history and allegedly leaked more reference tracks; Drake's Nov 2024 UMG/Spotify petition (withdrawn Jan 14, 2025) and Jan 15, 2025 defamation suit over "Not Like Us". [Complex timeline](https://www.complex.com/music/a/complex/a-timeline-of-alleged-drake-reference-tracks-leaking); [Wikipedia/SSS4U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Sexy_Songs_4_U)

---

## 2) The core repeatable workflow/formula (idea → finished master)

Synthesized from producer/engineer interviews and Drake's own accounts. This is the pattern that recurs across *every* era, including 2020-2025:

**Step 1 — Beats come to him, batch-style.** Drake doesn't sit with producers making beats; producers send packs. Gordo: Drake's request is literally "send me some stuff"; Gordo + collaborators (Richard Zestenker, Johannes Klahr) made **10-18 beats** for one song ("Rich Baby Daddy") and shipped them. Boi-1da: "I may pull up stuff and Drake will pick something or he'll have something he wants me to work on." [Complex/Gordo](https://www.complex.com/music/a/j-mckinney/gordo-drake-for-all-the-dogs-interview); [REVOLT/Boi-1da](https://www.revolt.tv/article/2021-10-28/126267/studio-sessions-boi-1da-talks-making-hits-with-drake-nfts-and-his-upcoming-album)

**Step 2 — The silent audition.** "The process is sending him stuff and him not saying anything and then sending him stuff and him being like, 'oh my God, this is it.'" (Gordo). Boi-1da: he never suggests anything to Drake — "you just give him what he needs and it's over from there." High rejection, instant acceptance. [Complex/Gordo](https://www.complex.com/music/a/j-mckinney/gordo-drake-for-all-the-dogs-interview); [REVOLT/Boi-1da](https://www.revolt.tv/article/2021-10-28/126267/studio-sessions-boi-1da-talks-making-hits-with-drake-nfts-and-his-upcoming-album)

**Step 3 — Melody + hook + first verse in one sitting, same night.** The beat arrives → Drake records immediately. Gordo made "Sticky" on a plane, texted Drake, and "by the time he replied at 4pm I was already in the kitchen at his house. I played him the beat and he was like, 'Woah'... **They recorded that night.**" [GQ/Gordo](https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/culture/article/drake-honestly-nevermind-gordo-club-music-influences). Same pattern in 2012: "The Motto" — T-Minus voice-clipped him a beat, Drake "did the verse and I did the hook" on the spot. [Rap Radar/RESPECT 2012](https://rapradarpodcast.substack.com/p/lost-words-2012-drake-talks-take). God's Plan: "a song that I recorded on a whim in my condo... I only had the first verse and the hook." [HowToRap transcription](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)

**Step 4 — Solo writing, machine pace.** Gordo: "He usually just locks himself up and does everything by himself. And in the studio he just does everything and then **you just wake up and he does like five songs in one night**... He's a mad man. He doesn't sleep... He'll call me at 9 a.m., 10 a.m. in the morning." [Complex/Gordo](https://www.complex.com/music/a/j-mckinney/gordo-drake-for-all-the-dogs-interview)

**Step 5 — Low discard rate; the demo unit is hook + verse.** "If I'm gonna go as far as to track over a beat I usually have the utmost faith in it that it'll end up somewhere. I don't really dispose of too many songs" (Drake, 2013). God's Plan leaked with only a hook + verse and Drake "had to rush and turn it around" — the song was finished because the room demanded it. [HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)

**Step 6 — The room test.** After laying a record, Drake plays it loud and watches: "the girls that just walked in the room. Are they going to start dancing to it right when they walk in? Do my friends already know the lyrics if I played it like six, seven times? Just little things, so I know this might be one of those ones." [Rap Radar/RESPECT 2012](https://rapradarpodcast.substack.com/p/lost-words-2012-drake-talks-take)

**Step 7 — Features and finishes are last-minute.** "First Person Shooter" was **recorded October 5, 2023 — the day before *For All the Dogs* dropped**; Drake confirmed J. Cole's verse hours before release ("fourth quarter magic", "we just got out from the studio"). [Wikipedia/FPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Person_Shooter_(song)). Album structure is decided late: he moved "Needle" (Nicki Minaj) off FATD because it didn't fit sonically. [Wikipedia/FATD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs)

**Step 8 — Engineering chain (fixed team):** Noel Cadastre records; **40 mixes** (Her Loss credits: 40 mixed every track; the album was delayed when 40 got COVID mid-mix); Chris Athens masters. SSS4U is the first Drake album **without 40 at all** — recorded mostly at Sanctuary Studios (Nassau) and S.O.T.A. (Florida/Toronto). [Wikipedia/Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss); [Wikipedia/SSS4U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Sexy_Songs_4_U)

**Step 9 — Ship fast, on cultural timing.** Surprise drops (HN, DLDT), holiday-aligned drops (Valentine's Day SSS4U), and tour-adjacent albums (FATD "developed mostly during the It's All a Blur Tour"). [Wikipedia/FATD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs)

**The rotating team (per-album evidence):** CLB: 40, Nineteen85, PartyNextDoor, OZ, Vinylz, Metro Boomin, TM88, WondaGurl, Travis Scott. HN: Gordo (6 tracks), 40, Black Coffee (exec), &Me, Rampa, Klahr. Her Loss: Boi-1da, Metro Boomin, OZ, Tay Keith, Vinylz, Wheezy, F1lthy, Lil Yachty. FATD: 40, Boi-1da, Sango, Southside, Bnyx, Gordo, Lil Yachty, OZ, The Alchemist, Conductor Williams, DJ Screw (posthumous). SSS4U: PartyNextDoor, Noel Cadastre, Gordo, Jordan Ullman (Majid Jordan), Elkan, Niketaz. [Wikipedia album pages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy)

---

## 3) Lyric method

- **Top-down, phrase-first.** Every 2020-2025 hit's hook is a repeated catchphrase that functions as the song's title: "Slime You Out", "First Person Shooter", "Rich Baby Daddy", "Nokia", "Gimme a Hug", "Toosie Slide", "Way 2 Sexy", "Rich Flex", "Jimmy Cooks". The hook line is the seed; verses fill around it.
- **Conversational direct address, not literature.** Drake writes to a "you" (usually a woman, sometimes the industry): low metaphor density, real-time thought ("stream of consciousness"), brand names and memes as texture. Critics have flagged the shallowness openly — Rolling Stone on FPS called his bars "desultory lyrics where he discusses women like he's stocking a meat freezer." [Rolling Stone](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/drake-for-all-the-dogs-review-1234848477/). The words are optimized to ride the melody, not to read well on Genius.
- **Writes on his phone, in the booth, not on paper.** 2010: "It shouldn't be your tagline, I don't even write... It's an individual creative process, there's no standard... **I'll pull out my phone and do that in front of everybody.** It's just about quality man and taking pride in yourself." [MTV 2010 via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c). Corroborated by the "whim" origin of God's Plan and "The Motto" (verse + hook written in the room in minutes).
- **Never repeats himself sonically.** "I don't wanna sound like No New Friends, I don't wanna sound like I'm On One. I did that already." (CRWN, 2015). Each project requires a new lane — which explains the genre-hopping: R&B-trap (CLB), house (HN), Atlanta drill (Her Loss), Miami bass (FATD), ringtone-pop (SSS4U). [CRWN via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **Emotion is the quality gate, not craft.** "There's points where you feel something and that's all that matters to me, that it penetrates." [Q TV 2013 via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **Inner-circle input.** Rich Paul pushed "Best I Ever Had" as the first single; manager Oliver El-Khatib feeds him playlists ("He gives me music that no-one else listens to, so that music combined with the extreme hood shit that I listen to like Lil Herb... I balance it all out"). [CRWN via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **Revision discipline: low.** Documented approach is fast completion, not iteration: "A lot of my hit songs I've written in a very short period of time. 'Hold On, We're Going Home,' I felt like we finished that in like two hours." When something is wrong he *knows* and scraps it rather than fixing it: "A lot of artists don't even know when they sound wrong, or off... if you don't know when something's wrong, you're not gonna be one of the greats." [MTV 2010 via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **Collab/credit reality (documented facts, no taboos):**
  - 2011: public whispers that The Weeknd's *House of Balloons* material fed *Take Care*. [Complex timeline](https://www.complex.com/music/a/complex/a-timeline-of-alleged-drake-reference-tracks-leaking)
  - July 22, 2015: Meek Mill tweeted "Stop comparing drake to me too…. He don't write his own raps! That's why he ain't tweet my album because we found out!" [Complex timeline](https://www.complex.com/music/a/complex/a-timeline-of-alleged-drake-reference-tracks-leaking)
  - Quentin Miller is **credited** as a writer on IYRTITL tracks ("10 Bands", "Know Yourself", "6 Man") — that's why 40 called him a co-writer, not a ghost. But Miller is **NOT credited on "R.I.C.O."** (Meek's album liner notes) despite laying a reference track for Drake's verse over the same beat — Complex's documented finding: "This evidence suggests that the description of Quentin Miller as a 'ghostwriter' is, indeed, accurate, despite OVO's claims to the contrary." [Complex credits investigation](https://www.complex.com/music/a/justin-charity/drake-quentin-miller-meek-mill-rico-liner-notes)
  - Funkmaster Flex premiered alleged Miller reference tracks for "10 Bands" (July 23, 2015), then "R.I.C.O."/"Used To"/"Know Yourself" (July 30, 2015). [Complex timeline](https://www.complex.com/music/a/complex/a-timeline-of-alleged-drake-reference-tracks-leaking); [Beats Boxing Mayhem](https://beatsboxingmayhem.com/2015/07/30/funkmaster-flex-releases-quentin-miller-reference-tracks-for-r-i-c-o-x-used-to-x-know-yourself/)
  - Miller's own account (VladTV, 2022, resurfaced 2024): he wrote on 5+ IYRTITL tracks and Drake's "R.I.C.O." verse; only DJ Drama and Drake knew; he claims he was never paid ("I never got a penny for all the Drake songs I wrote") and that a $30k publishing advance with Tricky Stewart trapped him. [VladTV headline](https://www.vladtv.com/article/290388/quentin-miller-i-never-got-a-penny-for-all-the-drake-songs-i-wrote); [Sportskeeda summary of clips](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/music/did-quentin-miller-write-lyrics-drake-s-songs-details-explored-clips-surface-ghostwriter-explaining-writing-relationship-drizzy)
  - 2018: Pusha T, "Infrared": "It was written like Nas but it came from Quentin." [FADER](https://www.thefader.com/2018/05/24/pusha-t-drake-ghostwriting-infrared-quentin-miller)
  - 2024: Complex's timeline counts **four alleged reference-track leaks in 2024 alone** (two in the final week before the article) as the Kendrick beef reignited the discourse; Kendrick's "Like That" (Mar 2024) answered J. ## 4) Topline / singing method (how the hook is built and sung)

- **Melody over minor-key beds.** "I do shy away from major, like major chords, major chord progressions. Those are the classic pop, those aren't the melodies that hit you in your heart. For me, it's minor. 40 produces in minor and I'll find the melodies to slip around it." - **The "Drake melody" device:** a short phrase repeated 2-4x with a tiny melodic arc (usually 2-3 notes), delivered in a sing-speak hybrid — rhythm like speech, pitch like a nursery rhyme, so the listener can reproduce it after one play. Examples: "Slime You Out" (title phrase as descending refrain), "Rich Baby Daddy" (chant-title + Sexyy Red's "Looking for the Hoes" interpolation), "Nokia" (the ringtone's 3-note motif sung/rapped over an Atlanta bass beat), "Toosie Slide" ("Slide, slide, slide" as dance instruction), "Way 2 Sexy" (Right Said Fred's chorus sung straight). - **Lazy, conversational delivery as the default.** Chest-voice half-singing with murmured, off-the-beat phrasing; he snaps into full singing for emotional peaks (the SZA duet sections, HN's dance tracks, "Nokia"'s second half where "the beat stutters and slows into a crunchy groove and Drake raps in a Whodini-type flow"). Cole + 7 producers/sample writers); "Rich Baby Daddy" has 13 (including Florence Welch and Isabella Summers for the interpolation). ## 8) "The trick" in their words

**Drake's own statement of the trick** (closest thing he's said to a formula, Q TV 2013): **make the melody slip around a minor-key bed and make it penetrate emotionally** — "Is anything too sugary? It just has to have emotion behind it... that it penetrates." Combined with his other recurring principle: **know instantly when it's right, don't overthink, record fast** — "A lot of this is organic, it's not that calculated" (God's Plan).

**Is it repeatable?** Yes — and the evidence is the record run itself: the same skeleton (minor beat → short repeated hook phrase → sung/rapped same night → room test → fast release) produced 7 No. 1s and ~40 top-10s in 2020-2025. What is *not* replicable is the layer underneath: a decade-deep producer bench, instant cultural-timing release machinery, and a catalogue that makes every drop an event. Gordo's formulation of the actual mechanic: "send him stuff and him not saying anything and then... 'oh my God, this is it'" — i.e., the bar is brutal, and once it clears, the song is finished in hours, not weeks.

## 2) The core repeatable workflow/formula (idea → finished master)

Synthesized from producer/engineer interviews and Drake's own accounts. This is the pattern that recurs across *every* era, including 2020-2025:

**Step 1 — Beats come to him, batch-style.** Drake doesn't sit with producers making beats; producers send packs. Gordo: Drake's request is literally "send me some stuff"; Gordo + collaborators (Richard Zestenker, Johannes Klahr) made **10-18 beats** for one song ("Rich Baby Daddy") and shipped them. Boi-1da: "I may pull up stuff and Drake will pick something or he'll have something he wants me to work on." [Complex/Gordo](https://www.complex.com/music/a/j-mckinney/gordo-drake-for-all-the-dogs-interview); [REVOLT/Boi-1da](https://www.revolt.tv/article/2021-10-28/126267/studio-sessions-boi-1da-talks-making-hits-with-drake-nfts-and-his-upcoming-album)

**Step 2 — The silent audition.** "The process is sending him stuff and him not saying anything and then sending him stuff and him being like, 'oh my God, this is it.'" (Gordo). Boi-1da: he never suggests anything to Drake — "you just give him what he needs and it's over from there." High rejection, instant acceptance. [Complex/Gordo](https://www.complex.com/music/a/j-mckinney/gordo-drake-for-all-the-dogs-interview); [REVOLT/Boi-1da](https://www.revolt.tv/article/2021-10-28/126267/studio-sessions-boi-1da-talks-making-hits-with-drake-nfts-and-his-upcoming-album)

**Step 3 — Melody + hook + first verse in one sitting, same night.** The beat arrives → Drake records immediately. Gordo made "Sticky" on a plane, texted Drake, and "by the time he replied at 4pm I was already in the kitchen at his house. I played him the beat and he was like, 'Woah'... **They recorded that night.**" [GQ/Gordo](https://www.gq-magazine.co.uk/culture/article/drake-honestly-nevermind-gordo-club-music-influences). Same pattern in 2012: "The Motto" — T-Minus voice-clipped him a beat, Drake "did the verse and I did the hook" on the spot. [Rap Radar/RESPECT 2012](https://rapradarpodcast.substack.com/p/lost-words-2012-drake-talks-take). God's Plan: "a song that I recorded on a whim in my condo... I only had the first verse and the hook." [HowToRap transcription](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)

**Step 4 — Solo writing, machine pace.** Gordo: "He usually just locks himself up and does everything by himself. And in the studio he just does everything and then **you just wake up and he does like five songs in one night**... He's a mad man. He doesn't sleep... He'll call me at 9 a.m., 10 a.m. in the morning." [Complex/Gordo](https://www.complex.com/music/a/j-mckinney/gordo-drake-for-all-the-dogs-interview)

**Step 5 — Low discard rate; the demo unit is hook + verse.** "If I'm gonna go as far as to track over a beat I usually have the utmost faith in it that it'll end up somewhere. I don't really dispose of too many songs" (Drake, 2013). God's Plan leaked with only a hook + verse and Drake "had to rush and turn it around" — the song was finished because the room demanded it. [HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)

**Step 6 — The room test.** After laying a record, Drake plays it loud and watches: "the girls that just walked in the room. Are they going to start dancing to it right when they walk in? Do my friends already know the lyrics if I played it like six, seven times? Just little things, so I know this might be one of those ones." [Rap Radar/RESPECT 2012](https://rapradarpodcast.substack.com/p/lost-words-2012-drake-talks-take)

**Step 7 — Features and finishes are last-minute.** "First Person Shooter" was **recorded October 5, 2023 — the day before *For All the Dogs* dropped**; Drake confirmed J. Cole's verse hours before release ("fourth quarter magic", "we just got out from the studio"). [Wikipedia/FPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Person_Shooter_(song)). Album structure is decided late: he moved "Needle" (Nicki Minaj) off FATD because it didn't fit sonically. [Wikipedia/FATD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs)

**Step 8 — Engineering chain (fixed team):** Noel Cadastre records; **40 mixes** (Her Loss credits: 40 mixed every track; the album was delayed when 40 got COVID mid-mix); Chris Athens masters. SSS4U is the first Drake album **without 40 at all** — recorded mostly at Sanctuary Studios (Nassau) and S.O.T.A. (Florida/Toronto). [Wikipedia/Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss); [Wikipedia/SSS4U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Sexy_Songs_4_U)

**Step 9 — Ship fast, on cultural timing.** Surprise drops (HN, DLDT), holiday-aligned drops (Valentine's Day SSS4U), and tour-adjacent albums (FATD "developed mostly during the It's All a Blur Tour"). [Wikipedia/FATD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs)

**The rotating team (per-album evidence):** CLB: 40, Nineteen85, PartyNextDoor, OZ, Vinylz, Metro Boomin, TM88, WondaGurl, Travis Scott. HN: Gordo (6 tracks), 40, Black Coffee (exec), &Me, Rampa, Klahr. Her Loss: Boi-1da, Metro Boomin, OZ, Tay Keith, Vinylz, Wheezy, F1lthy, Lil Yachty. FATD: 40, Boi-1da, Sango, Southside, Bnyx, Gordo, Lil Yachty, OZ, The Alchemist, Conductor Williams, DJ Screw (posthumous). SSS4U: PartyNextDoor, Noel Cadastre, Gordo, Jordan Ullman (Majid Jordan), Elkan, Niketaz. [Wikipedia album pages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy)

## 3) Lyric method

- **Top-down, phrase-first.** Every 2020-2025 hit's hook is a repeated catchphrase that functions as the song's title: "Slime You Out", "First Person Shooter", "Rich Baby Daddy", "Nokia", "Gimme a Hug", "Toosie Slide", "Way 2 Sexy", "Rich Flex", "Jimmy Cooks". The hook line is the seed; verses fill around it.
- **Conversational direct address, not literature.** Drake writes to a "you" (usually a woman, sometimes the industry): low metaphor density, real-time thought ("stream of consciousness"), brand names and memes as texture. Critics have flagged the shallowness openly — Rolling Stone on FPS called his bars "desultory lyrics where he discusses women like he's stocking a meat freezer." [Rolling Stone](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/drake-for-all-the-dogs-review-1234848477/). The words are optimized to ride the melody, not to read well on Genius.
- **Writes on his phone, in the booth, not on paper.** 2010: "It shouldn't be your tagline, I don't even write... It's an individual creative process, there's no standard... **I'll pull out my phone and do that in front of everybody.** It's just about quality man and taking pride in yourself." [MTV 2010 via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c). Corroborated by the "whim" origin of God's Plan and "The Motto" (verse + hook written in the room in minutes).
- **Never repeats himself sonically.** "I don't wanna sound like No New Friends, I don't wanna sound like I'm On One. I did that already." (CRWN, 2015). Each project requires a new lane — which explains the genre-hopping: R&B-trap (CLB), house (HN), Atlanta drill (Her Loss), Miami bass (FATD), ringtone-pop (SSS4U). [CRWN via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **Emotion is the quality gate, not craft.** "There's points where you feel something and that's all that matters to me, that it penetrates." [Q TV 2013 via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **Inner-circle input.** Rich Paul pushed "Best I Ever Had" as the first single; manager Oliver El-Khatib feeds him playlists ("He gives me music that no-one else listens to, so that music combined with the extreme hood shit that I listen to like Lil Herb... I balance it all out"). [CRWN via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **Revision discipline: low.** Documented approach is fast completion, not iteration: "A lot of my hit songs I've written in a very short period of time. 'Hold On, We're Going Home,' I felt like we finished that in like two hours." When something is wrong he *knows* and scraps it rather than fixing it: "A lot of artists don't even know when they sound wrong, or off... if you don't know when something's wrong, you're not gonna be one of the greats." [MTV 2010 via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **Collab/credit reality (documented facts, no taboos):**
  - 2011: public whispers that The Weeknd's *House of Balloons* material fed *Take Care*. [Complex timeline](https://www.complex.com/music/a/complex/a-timeline-of-alleged-drake-reference-tracks-leaking)
  - July 22, 2015: Meek Mill tweeted "Stop comparing drake to me too…. He don't write his own raps! That's why he ain't tweet my album because we found out!" [Complex timeline](https://www.complex.com/music/a/complex/a-timeline-of-alleged-drake-reference-tracks-leaking)
  - Quentin Miller is **credited** as a writer on IYRTITL tracks ("10 Bands", "Know Yourself", "6 Man") — that's why 40 called him a co-writer, not a ghost. But Miller is **NOT credited on "R.I.C.O."** (Meek's album liner notes) despite laying a reference track for Drake's verse over the same beat — Complex's documented finding: "This evidence suggests that the description of Quentin Miller as a 'ghostwriter' is, indeed, accurate, despite OVO's claims to the contrary." ## 4) Topline / singing method (how the hook is built and sung)

- **Melody over minor-key beds.** "I do shy away from major, like major chords, major chord progressions. Those are the classic pop, those aren't the melodies that hit you in your heart. For me, it's minor. 40 produces in minor and I'll find the melodies to slip around it." [Q TV 2013 via HowToRap](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **The "Drake melody" device:** a short phrase repeated 2-4x with a tiny melodic arc (usually 2-3 notes), delivered in a sing-speak hybrid — rhythm like speech, pitch like a nursery rhyme, so the listener can reproduce it after one play. Examples: "Slime You Out" (title phrase as descending refrain), "Rich Baby Daddy" (chant-title + Sexyy Red's "Looking for the Hoes" interpolation), "Nokia" (the ringtone's 3-note motif sung/rapped over an Atlanta bass beat), "Toosie Slide" ("Slide, slide, slide" as dance instruction), "Way 2 Sexy" (Right Said Fred's chorus sung straight). Hooks are built to be bellowed back at stadiums. [HowToRap analysis](https://medium.com/@HowToRap/drake-teaches-how-to-write-a-melody-in-3-steps-7fb12d2f427c)
- **Lazy, conversational delivery as the default.** Chest-voice half-singing with murmured, off-the-beat phrasing; he snaps into full singing for emotional peaks (the SZA duet sections, HN's dance tracks, "Nokia"'s second half where "the beat stutters and slows into a crunchy groove and Drake raps in a Whodini-type flow"). [Pitchfork on Nokia](https://pitchfork.com/reviews/tracks/drake-partynextdoor-nokia/)
- **Pre-proven melodies as hooks.** A core 2020-2025 trick: anchor the hook on a melody the public already knows — Right Said Fred ("Way 2 Sexy"), Florence + the Machine's "Dog Days Are Over" ("Rich Baby Daddy"), the Nokia ringtone ("Nokia"), Daft Punk's "One More Time" ("Circo Loco"), K.P. & Envyi's "Swing My Way" as the bounce blueprint for "Rich Baby Daddy" (Gordo: "I was like, no one's done that in a long time"). [Complex/Gordo](https://www.complex.com/music/a/j-mckinney/gordo-drake-for-all-the-dogs-interview); [Wikipedia/Rich Baby Daddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Baby_Daddy)
- **Vocal texture:** doubled/layered choruses and ad-libbed asides are audible on the records (observable, not producer-documented in this run); heavy autotune as an *instrument* on HN/SSS4U (observable). Producer Elkan contributes "androgynous vocals" and background vocals on "Nokia" to thicken the top line. [Wikipedia/Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_(song))
- **The writer-count tells the story:** "Nokia" has exactly **2 writers** (Drake + Elkan) — one singer, one beatmaker, no co-writer room; "First Person Shooter" has 9 writers (Drake, J. Cole + 7 producers/sample writers); "Rich Baby Daddy" has 13 (including Florence Welch and Isabella Summers for the interpolation). Toplines are Drake's; credits balloon with sample/interpolation rights and producer contributions. [Wikipedia/Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_(song)); [Wikipedia/FPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Person_Shooter_(song)); [Wikipedia/Rich Baby Daddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rich_Baby_Daddy)

## 5) Vocal-anchoring production (what the track does around the vocal)

Brief — production only as scaffolding for the hook:

- **Sparse, minor, sample-based beds that leave air for the voice.** Drake's description of 40's method: "He wouldn't just let a beat sit. I would leave the studio and by the time I came back the next day, he'd be like 'I added some shit'... He's just been so amazing at making a piece grow or shrink... He was the mastermind behind the music." [VIBE 2013](https://www.vibe.com/gallery/outtakes-drake-talks-beyonce-trophies-and-next-album/)
- **One famous melodic element + one groove, then get out of the way.** "Slime You Out": a looped "Just Ask Me" (The Soul Superbs) vocal sample with soft drums so the Drake/SZA duet sits on top. "First Person Shooter": warped Joe Washington vocal sample + a down-pitched orchestral loop ("Redemption"), with a beat switch to host two rappers. "Nokia": flashy synth (the ringtone) + "sweaty Atlanta bass beat" (Pitchfork). "Rich Baby Daddy": Miami-bass bounce interpolating "Dog Days Are Over". [Wikipedia/Slime You Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slime_You_Out); [Wikipedia/FPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Person_Shooter_(song)); [Pitchfork](https://pitchfork.com/reviews/tracks/drake-partynextdoor-nokia/)
- **The mix is the finish line, and it's 40's.** Her Loss's official delay reason was 40 contracting COVID during mixing/mastering; Chris Athens masters. [Wikipedia/Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss); [Wikipedia/Nokia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_(song))
